015d7fdc1cb1.title: Hand back to the discussion
015d7fdc1cb1.content: Skill hand-back-to-discussion: A sibling agent, spawned during or working beside a live agent-human discussion, hands every card, question, decision, result, blocker or piece of context back to the discussion agent that is talking with the person, and never leaves it only in its own thread. The discussion agent asks the person (ask-the-person), marks every copy answered, and routes the answer back. A review sheet or issue in play is an extra channel. Use whenever an agent that is not the one talking with the person has something the person must see. Named by: Ask the person, Hand back to the discussion . The procedure behind Process_HandBackToDiscussion. It joins two rules that already bind: ask-the-person (how a question is put) and the relay paragraph of interaction-modality §4.1 (a relayed question says where the answer goes). This skill is the missing step between them: who puts the question, and how the answer gets back.

3b7432360588.title: Why
3b7432360588.content: A card posted only in a sibling’s own thread is not seen by the person, who is talking with the discussion agent elsewhere; the decision stalls, or reaches the person only by reconstruction. A feedback channel in play (a review sheet, an issue) is used as well.

61e0e853ff52.title: The two roles
61e0e853ff52.content: | role | who | does | . | Discussion agent (session-coordinator) | the agent the person is talking with right now: a project coordinator, the parent of a subagent, the session that spawned a swarm | shows the hand-back to the person, asks with ask-the-person, marks every copy answered, routes the answer back | . | Sibling (sibling-session) | any agent the discussion agent spawned, or one working beside it on the same goal: a project thread, a subagent, a workflow agent, a cloud session | composes the hand-back once, with the analysis it alone has, and acts on the answer | . You are a sibling when your brief names a discussion agent, or when you were started by another agent while a person was talking with it. A sibling that is not sure hands back anyway: one extra copy costs a line, and a missed card costs a stalled decision.

881eae87be5a.title: The brief names the discussion (spawning agent)
881eae87be5a.content: An agent that spawns a sibling during a live discussion puts the discussion link in the brief (definitions.discussion of the input schema): who the discussion agent is, how to reach it, the standing card rules, and any feedback channel in play (a review sheet’s id and tab, an issue). See process-state §”A coordinator that briefs a thread”. A sibling has nothing else that tells it.

d46b818cf7ee.title: Input and output
d46b818cf7ee.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In (the hand-back): from (title, link, process), to (the discussion link), kind (decision, question, context, result, blocker), a one-sentence summary, ask (the ask-the-person input, unchanged, for a decision or question), context (for the others), links, channels (always discussion, plus any of own-thread, project-chat, review-sheet, github-issue, github-pr), answerRoute, blocking, and supersedes when it replaces an earlier one. | Out (the record): shown (every copy, discussion first), state (open, answered, withdrawn, superseded, informed), the ask-the-person output, chosen, quote, answeredIn, marked (the strike-through edit per copy) and deliveredBack (proof the answer reached the sibling, with citesPerson). | .

3679411c082f.title: Steps — sibling
3679411c082f.content: . | Compose once. A question is the full ask-the-person input: what will differ, context, every option lettered with a one-line trade-off, the recommendation and why, what happens with no answer. The discussion agent must be able to show it without opening your thread. Context, a result or a blocker gets the same test. | Show it where you are. Post it in your own thread too (chat text, then the card), so the tappable card sits beside the work. Your own thread is never the only copy. | Mirror it to the feedback channel in play. When a review sheet governs the work, write the “Decision needed” block into the row’s agent column and set Agentic status to Needs you (the document layer’s review-sheet-script skill, §”A question to people goes in the sheet”). An issue or PR in play gets a comment. These are extra copies, never instead of the discussion. | Hand back to the discussion agent with the host’s route: . | host | route | . | Claude projects thread | message_coordinator (or message_thread to the discussion thread), the hand-back as plain prose in the schema’s order: summary, question, lettered options with trade-offs, recommendation, if silent, link to your thread | . | subagent (Agent tool, workflow agent) | your final report: the hand-back as a fenced json block that validates against the input schema, then a one-line summary. You cannot reach the person; the parent asks | . | sibling session | SendMessage to the discussion session | . | none of these | a comment on the issue or PR the discussion is about, and say so in your own thread | . | Keep working on the recommended option where it can be undone; stop where it cannot (blocking: true). | Act on the answer when it comes back. Only an answer that carries the person’s own words (a cited message, a card tap, a Blue-column cell) is their approval. A paraphrase from another agent is not. | .

77c89e490f6d.title: Steps — discussion agent
77c89e490f6d.content: . | Show it in the discussion, saying it comes from the sibling (title and link) and that you will pass the answer on. A question goes through Process_AskThePerson unchanged: the chat text in full first, then the card with the same letters. Never “see the card in thread X”. | Context, a result or a blocker that needs no answer: post it, state informed, done. | Take the answer from any copy. A tap on your card, a tap on the sibling’s card, or a Blue-column answer in the sheet all count. Take the first, and treat a later disagreeing answer as a new question. | Route it back on answerRoute, attaching the person’s own message by id where the host allows (citesPerson: true). | Mark every copy answered. A chat copy keeps its text: strike the question through and add [Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]. A card you posted is closed with the chosen option. A sheet’s “Decision needed” block is replaced by the decision and who made it, and Agentic status moves on. A withdrawn or superseded hand-back is marked the same way with the reason. | A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn (symbiotic-interaction §2). | .

6728442f266d.title: Anti-patterns
6728442f266d.content: . | A card only in the sibling’s thread. | A hand-back that says “see my thread”. A pointer is not the question. | The discussion agent rewriting the options. The sibling did the analysis; reword for the person if needed, but keep the letters and the recommendation, and say so if you change one. | The sheet as the only copy. People on the committee see the sheet; the owner in the discussion may not be looking at it. | An answer that never reaches the sibling. The person answered once; the sibling must not ask again. | .

5f8b518853b3.content: What this skill takes and gives, as a class diagram drawn from its JSON Schema contracts by the schemas viewer’s own renderer. 9c76609fb6c8.title: Hand back to the discussion
9c76609fb6c8.content: Process_HandBackToDiscussion · strict · 8 step(s) . How a sibling agent gets a card, question, result, blocker or context in front of the person: through the discussion agent that is talking with them, never only in its own thread. The person’s answer comes back the same way. INPUT AND OUTPUT: the hand-back-to-discussion skill’s schemas, schemas/skills/hand-back-to-discussion/input.schema.json (from, to, kind, summary, ask = the ask-the-person input, context, links, channels, answerRoute, blocking) and output.schema.json (shown, state, chosen, quote, answeredIn, marked, deliveredBack). THE PERSON’S STEP is inside Process_AskThePerson, called by the discussion agent, so the asking rule (chat text first, then the card) holds here unchanged. A Blue-column answer in a review sheet is an answer to that same question. i i i i i i i i

8f1a6564fb6e.title: A harness’s default rendering
8f1a6564fb6e.content: Process_HarnessRendering · strict · 8 step(s) . Renders a harness layer as its default interface: its left-hand nav and docs on its own theme’s art, and a board of its todos and beans from which a reader reads, reviews and, when a write tool is available, proposes changes into the publication review. The theme art goes behind every docs page. Read-only is the floor. Whether the reader may write is a question about the tools the session has (git-push, github-api, github-connector) and the reader’s permissions, so the gateway reads capabilities and never assumes one write path. A change a reader proposes enters the content change review in folio-assistant-core (content-change-review.bpmn); this process enables that review and does not replace it. i i i i i i i i

9702b98a736f.title: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
9702b98a736f.content: Skill harness-projections: Who may write under .claude/, and when. The generated projections of the knowledge graph (.claude/commands/*.md from skill:commands, the assembled agent memory under .claude/agents/ and .claude/agent-memory/) are written by CI, which commits them to the PR branch, and never by an agent. A hand-edited .claude/ file (settings.json, its hooks, a hand-written command or agent definition) changes only with the owner’s explicit consent to that change: the agent shows the exact diff and the reason, asks first, and records the consent. Read before staging any path under .claude/. Named by: Human Translation Workflow, Translation review and adjudication, Cut over to the separated graph, Move the graph into its repositories, Prepare a graph to stand alone, KG to public portal, Remote-mount a dependency, Mount a declared subgraph, Build and publish a per-slice SQLite file, A sub-KG is staged in place, then leaves for its own repository, Actor and role administration, Render a Knowledge Graph to a CDN, Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it, A harness’s default rendering, Render log — the publish branch keeps its own history, Publish a web app — declared, translated, built at its own route, An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, An IG release: the owner tags, a draft is built, the owner publishes, Questionnaire wireframe review, Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs, Review and publish a folio, IRIS CDN initial load, IRIS CDN nightly change ingest, IRIS CDN weekly reconciliation, Sign and publish an IRIS CDN release .claude/ is what the Claude Code harness reads before any skill is loaded: the slash commands a person can type, the memory injected into a subagent, and the hooks and permissions every session runs under. An edit there changes how every later session behaves, including sessions that never see the commit.claude/ is one instance of a general rule. Every coding-agent Tool has config files, and some of them are projections of the graph: CI writes the projections, and a person consents to each hand edit.claude/ is named here because it is the agent-host directory the generators write. Which files a Tool reads, and which of them are generated, belongs to that Tool’s adapter. Securing what the agent may do at all is agent-permissions.

ec0733208814.title: Two kinds of file, two writers
ec0733208814.content: | kind | examples | source of truth | who writes the .claude/ file | . | projection (generated) | .claude/commands/<name>.md carrying a generated: key (skill:commands); the marked region of .claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md (agent-memory); .claude/agents/* where the memory assembler writes them; .claude/skills/ synced from packages | the skill’s front matter, the memory nodes under memory/, the package | CI only. A workflow step runs the generator and commits the result to the PR branch. | . | hand-edited | .claude/settings.json and its hooks, a hand-written command (no generated: key), an agent definition’s hand-written body, a memory file’s ## Session log | the file itself | an agent, only with the owner’s consent to that exact change | . The rule for a projection: edit the source, not the projection. To change a slash command, change the skill’s user_invocable or description. To change what a subagent remembers, add or edit a node under memory/ (agent-memory). Push the source change and let CI write the projection. You may run a generator locally in its --check form, or into a scratch tree, to see what it would write. Do not stage or commit anything it writes under .claude/. This applies inside skill-registration too. skill:register runs skill:commands, which writes .claude/commands/ in a composed checkout. Commit what it writes everywhere else, and leave .claude/ to CI. Why CI and not the agent. A projection is correct only if it was generated from the tree that lands. An agent’s local run reflects the tree it had, and a hand-merged projection drifts from its source; the CI step runs on the PR head, so the projection on the branch is the one the merge will carry, from one writer.

835270f30566.title: Hand-edited files: consent per change
835270f30566.content: Before you write a hand-edited .claude/ file: . | Show the exact diff. Paste the unified diff itself, not a description of it. | Give the reason: what breaks or is missing without the change, and what the change does to every later session (a hook that runs on every tool call; a permission that stops a prompt). | Ask, and wait. The order is context, diff, recommendation, question (interaction-modality §4.1). “Go ahead” discharges this question, for this diff only. | Record the consent in the commit that makes the change, and as a comment on the PR: . claude-config-consent: by: <owner's login> on: <ISO-8601 date-time> file: .claude/settings.json diff: <sha256 of the diff shown> evidence: "<the owner's words, verbatim>" (<session link or comment permalink>) . | . A standing waiver does not reach this. Consent is per change, so there is no gate class for it in confirmation-waiver’s table, and a waiver that claims one is not a waiver. A broad instruction such as “fix the hooks” or “make the session start work” authorises the investigation. It does not authorise the edit. Bring the diff back. When a hook or setting gets in your way, report it; do not edit it. This is the same rule as prepare-merge §Guardrails (“fix the tool” rather than delete the branch), with one extra step: here, fixing the tool is itself a change that needs consent.

b0ec99749234.title: Where it sits in the process
b0ec99749234.content: merge-to-main.bpmn runs Task_RegenProjections in its build-pipeline lane before it reads any evidence. CI regenerates the projections on the head and commits them to the PR branch, and the evidence is then read on that new head. A PR whose projections are stale therefore cannot reach the merge gate looking green (merge-to-main (opt-in cat-harness.sdlc)).

That change is not made here. | No check refuses an agent-authored commit under .claude/. f83cf44fb897.title: A tile is the harness’s, not the node’s
f83cf44fb897.content: Skill harness-tiles: A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides. Named by: A harness’s default rendering, Board: open and close content, Board: relocate content to the trashcan . A tile is a function of a harness watching a directory, not of nodes. If a harness declares visualisers, each one gets a tile; a tile defaults to the theme, and a harness can declare one or more visualisations, each with a title. The tile set is not a new registry — it is the visualiser obligation made reachable. A harness declares its visualisers in its <instance>.json visualisers (HarnessVisualiserSchema), and kg:audit reports which directories owe one. A graph that owes a visualiser owes a tile, so the audit needs no second list free to disagree with it.

0b520e0bf175.title: Where a tile goes — the declared route, and nothing else
0b520e0bf175.content: Each visualiser is ONE declaration in the harness that owns it: . "visualisers": [ { "id": "library", "renderedBy": "library-viewer", "coversKinds": ["library"], "subgraphs": "instance" }, { "id": "todos", "renderedBy": "state-viewer", "covers": ["todos"], "alias": "todos" }, { "id": "fsh-guts", "renderedBy": "staging-graph-viewer", "covers": ["fsh-guts"], "publish": "staging-only", "writer": ["scripts/gen-fsh-guts-viz.ts"] } ] . | id is the URL segment; renderedBy names a Tool node (the implementation may live anywhere); covers names this harness’s own directory ids, coversKinds graph typologies, over every declared directory of them in the checkout. A harness never names another layer’s directory — that would be a lower layer naming a higher one. | The URL is computed, never chosen. visualiserRoute in schemas/kg/visualiser-route.ts is the ONE function every generator and reader uses: <harness>/<id>/ for the full KG, <harness>/<id>/<sub-graph>/ for one sub-graph (subgraphs: "instance" — one per covered layer — or "directory", nested under subgraphUnder[kind] where the visualiser declares one), and an asset path below either. Every page is written to that route under the site’s docs layer, so the file and the URL cannot disagree. A tile opens the sub-graph view when it exists, else the full one. | A page claims nothing. A page carries only rendered-by: <Tool>, as provenance; it carries no renders: or <meta name="renders">. A directory’s coverage.visualiser is filled IN MEMORY by withViewers from the declarations, never from disk. | Collisions are declaration errors. bun run cat check:visualiser-routes refuses two declarations resolving to one route (or one inside another’s subtree), a page drawn by a Tool outside every route that Tool is declared to render, a page under a route that names a different Tool, a visualiser covering a kind its Tool does not renders, and any renders: or coverage.visualiser on disk. | The short URL is an opt-in alias. alias: "todos" makes <base>/todos/ a redirect to <base>/cat-harness/todos/, composed by compose-docs.ts for every page under the route. An alias that names another alias, a harness, or anything the site already carries at its top level is refused by the gate before a build and by the composer during one. A tile always links the canonical route. | publish: "staging-only": compose-docs withholds the route (and its alias) from a canonical deploy. | .

66105962a21c.title: Instantiated is a different fact from declared
66105962a21c.content: Only the harnesses instantiated in the folio get tiles, not every dependency. Which layers are instantiated here is answered by the root index.config.json (instances[]), or without an index by each root <name>.config.json. That rule is index-config’s; the tiles only consume it, because the navbar cannot be derived from the declarations alone and a directory listing is not the question a reader is asking. Dependencies keep a group of their own rather than disappearing, so a reader looking for one is not answered with silence. A harness a KG subscription chose is instantiated by the same file, with no local declaration: its declaration is the substrate snapshot kg:subscribe cached at the pin. bun run cat kg:instantiate <subscription> <harness> writes the config and the harness’s state directories (and, under an index, the harness’s instances[] entry), and refuses a harness that was not chosen, not declared at the pin, or whose needs nothing here holds. The tile is drawn from the snapshot (scripts/subscribed-harnesses.ts): it links nowhere, because nothing of it is published here, and a snapshot that cannot be read is a finding on the tile rather than an empty one.

ce6f266ba032.title: Which harness / is — the landing is index-config’s rule
ce6f266ba032.content: The site’s landing page is one of the instantiated harnesses. It is never the layer the generator happens to live in, and never the repository’s name. Which one it is — site.landing in the root index.config.json (an layer name or "hub"), or the per-config site.landing flag without an index — is index-config’s rule. resolveLandingInstance in schemas/kg/harness-config.ts reads both, and check:landing-instance is the gate. When the landing is the neutral hub, / is the harness listing (harness_details.html, these tiles) and the todo panel — the landing sticky panel, not a second board.

49a3d75047eb.title: “Harness” carries TWO senses, and only one of them is this rule
49a3d75047eb.content: | sense | what it means | how you tell | . | 1 — instantiated here | this checkout runs it | an entry in the root index.config.json instances[] — or, in a folio with no index, a root <name>.config.json (index-config). Read the file, not a number quoted here | . | 2 — a layer others instantiate | a base a downstream repo stands up | nothing in this checkout. It is a statement about the layer’s role in the stack | . The rules on this page are about sense 1. Sense 2 is correct usage too: a layer can be declared, not instantiated, and declare no visualiser — so it owes no tile — while being exactly what a downstream repository instantiates. No count is given for either sense, because a count in prose is a claim nothing checks; ask the filesystem. Do not write a checker for this. A predicate on the word cannot separate its two senses, so it is an adjudication, not a check (adjudication). When the word is load-bearing, say which sense — “instantiated here” or “a layer downstream repos instantiate”.

bc48148487f0.title: A tile opens the LAYER, not a kind handler’s view of it
bc48148487f0.content: A viewer page is a RENDERING with its own IRI, separate from the asset it shows; see kg-viewer §”The asset and its rendering are two resources with two IRIs”. scripts/mount-instance-docs.ts carries the two routes: . | route | handler | what it is | . | /<kind>/<instance>/ | the kind’s, cat-harness’s | the default rendering any layer declaring that kind gets | . | /<instance>/ | the layer itself | its own themed root | . The tile’s target is the layer’s own themed root when it has one, and a handler’s viewer only when it does not. The viewers stay reachable, listed beneath. A layer has that root when it has its own site directory, read from its own declaration — never by probing the BUILT site, where a layer whose pages are generated at build time has none until its generator runs.

3fe6ced59115.title: Order is the declared dependency stack, reversed
3fe6ced59115.content: Bottom to top, computed from the declared needs, never written out as names: a name list is a rule true only for the layers somebody remembered. The spine’s head keeps the top and its floor keeps the bottom. A layer whose layer nobody declared is undetermined — placed below the head, alphabetically, carrying a finding that says its place is not derived. Absent is not []: one is nobody having said, the other is a layer asserting it sits on nothing. A broken graph does not blank the navbar. flattenDependencies returns an empty order on a cycle, which is right for a pipeline and wrong for a sidebar, where showing nothing hides every layer over one typo. The problems are reported and the list falls back to alphabetical.

ab89e3827537.title: Two gaps, reported rather than hidden
ab89e3827537.content: Both are the third state, and they are DIFFERENT findings: . | declared and not rendered — a graph the layer declares with no published page. Not linked (a dead link reads as “this site is broken”), and reported. | rendered and not declared — a page published under a kind the layer does not declare. Also not linked, because the declaration decides what a tile may claim to show — and reported, because staying silent would hide a working viewer behind a rule, and the remedy is one line in a declaration. | .

473e8507376c.title: An inert row SAYS why, and “no viewer” is four answers
473e8507376c.content: A declared graph with no published viewer appears in the navbar as a row that does not open. Drawing it grey is not saying it: . | A title on a non-focusable element is a label for a pointer and for nothing else — no keyboard path, and not reliably announced. | Dimming alone is state carried by contrast, and can pass the contrast ratio while saying nothing. | . The reason is content: real text in the row. It is in the accessibility tree, survives a stylesheet that does not load, and cannot disagree with a second signal. Do not use aria-disabled — nothing is a control, and marking a <span> disabled announces a widget that does not exist. “No viewer” is four states, told apart by inertNote (harness-tiles.ts): . | state | the row says | is it a gap? | . | declared publish: "staging-only" | staging only | no — withheld on purpose | . | layer declares renderExemption.of: ["visualiser"] | no viewer by design | no | . | a viewer exists off the conventional path | viewer not published | yes, and a different one | . | nothing declares a viewer | no viewer yet | yes | . One wording for all four would label an intended state a gap, which is as wrong as hiding a real gap. Neither navbar picks the words. They render what the generator gave them, which keeps them one navbar rather than two that agree by maintenance. A kind the generator said nothing about renders with no claim about why.

6a8ee56c9337.title: A tile, or an avatar? WHO DECLARED IT
6a8ee56c9337.content: A tile is what the HARNESS declares. An avatar is what the FOLIO holds. | the thing | renders as | because | . | a declared visualiser (the harness’s visualisers) — over a directory or sub-graph | tile, functional | the harness declares it; §”A tile is the harness’s” above | . | a set of schema instances — todos | tile, content | the harness declares the set; the instances are the folio’s | . | a note, a document, a materialised asset in the folio’s reproduce directories (library/, uploads/) | avatar | the folio holds it; it is the reader’s, not the harness’s | . A TILE IS ONE OF TWO KINDS, and they bind to different things . |   | functional tile | content tile | . | subject | a directory or sub-graph | a set of schema instances | . | bound to | a SKILL | a SCHEMA | . | resolved when opened | a tool that implements the skill | the instances | . | what empty means | a gap to report — a skill nothing implements is unreachable | a real state — “nothing outstanding” is not “broken” | . A functional tile names the SKILL, never the tool. schemas/tools/tool-types.ts makes tools that satisfy one skill interchangeable, so a tile bound to a tool breaks the moment another tool is chosen. Likewise VisualiserDeclarationSchema takes “one path, or several visualisations”: a sub-graph may be rendered more than one way. Empty is asymmetric. A content tile opening on zero instances is CORRECT and must not be hidden — an empty board and a person with nothing outstanding are opposite facts. A functional tile whose skill has no tool is a gap to report. THEME IS NOT A THIRD KIND. A theme is a palette and its art; a tile takes the avatar’s declared hue. Theme is how either one looks, never an alternative to being a tile. Size does not decide it . A whole materialised knowledge graph (such as cat-bootstrap or cat-harness) on the glass renders as an avatar. So these two tempting rules are wrong: . | “Many behind it → tile, one → avatar” — a materialised graph is many things and is an avatar. | “Opens a viewer over a set → tile” — opening that avatar opens a viewer over a set, and it is still an avatar. | . Declaration ownership decides: a materialised asset is in the reader’s folio however big it is. The same subject can be both. todos is a content tile in the strip and an individual todo is an avatar on the glass: the tile is bound to the SCHEMA and the avatar is one INSTANCE of it. What is checkable here, and what is not . Tile-vs-avatar is not. Nothing classifies a folio item; the rule governs authoring, and the renderer reads the graph an item came from, so a gate would be a declared property whose check cannot answer its own claim. “A functional tile names the skill, never the tool” IS: a declared visualisation naming a tool id where a skill name belongs is decidable against knownSkills() and the Tool graph. No such tile exists yet, so nothing is gated today.

b57cae24e398.title: The navbar icon row is DECLARED, and three states is not two
b57cae24e398.content: navbarIcons on the layer declaration. A closed set — close, todos, beans, processes, kg, fsh-guts, qr, launcher — because a free string lets a layer name an icon nothing draws. Seven is the cap and it is refused, never truncated: silently dropping an eighth entry would overrule the layer’s decision. fsh-guts is a control, like launcher: a button that opens the discarded-items list and carries its live count, not a link. It is also the way back the discard confirmation names, so that dialog says “the fish in the icon row” only when this icon is on the page, and points at Page settings otherwise (board-windows §”Send to fsh-guts asks first”). | declared | means | . | absent | inherit — walk needs, site owner as the floor | . | [] | show none | . | a list | this layer’s own answer | . Absent and [] must not collapse. The guard is !== undefined, never a truthiness test: a truthiness test turns “nobody has said” into “nothing to show”, and makes a layer that has not declared the field indistinguishable from one that wants a bare navbar. The distinction is kept at every layer: resolveNavbarIcons returns undefined for undetermined, harness-tiles.ts omits the field rather than writing [], sync-docs-harness.ts emits null, and the client draws no row and says so once. The walk is needs, not a second traversal. Nearest declaration wins, breadth-first toward the foundation — the direction resolveSkillDirs already composes. A new walk would be a second answer to “what is this layer built on”, free to disagree with the first. Destinations are looked up, never written down. They come from the layer’s own declared visualisations plus siteLinks, so an icon whose graph this layer does not publish gets no href and renders as a non-link. close and launcher carry no href on purpose: they drive controls on the page, and an href would make them look like navigation.

12ef9abcd39d.title: The theme avatar: the assignment is theme-mediated
12ef9abcd39d.content: The navbar’s mark is the layer’s theme card art, clipped — not its icon. The chain: . layer → its sticky contribution → the sticky’s theme → the theme’s imageRole → the layer’s images carrying that role → the card layout → its avatarRegion . resolveThemeBackdrop is the join and returns the DeclaredImage, so the crop comes with it. An indirection is not an absence: look through the theme before concluding no assignment exists. Take the card layout, not laptop or mobile. KgImageSchema refuses a non-square avatarRegion in pixels, and only the square crop can satisfy that: equal fractions on a landscape image give a box wider than tall, and the clip scales width and height separately. A card with no declared crop is a finding, not an avatar: the whole composition squeezed into a small frame is unreadable. Report it and fall back to the mark.

6b32a5765ee8.title: Where a tile lives, and what it must not eat
6b32a5765ee8.content: Tiles render in the navbar and on the glass: one declaration, per-surface visibility, never two registries. The sticky board carries NO tiles. | Removing a surface loses nothing only if the others still carry it. Every tile this repository declares names navbar and glass, so each stays reachable. A tile that named ONLY a surface that is not mounted would vanish silently — report it, do not re-route it on the author’s behalf. | board stays a legal value in TILE_SURFACES, and nothing mounts it, so existing declarations that name it stay valid (the “every field but ref is optional” rule in schemas/kg/cat-harness.ts). A declaration saying ["board"] alone is valid and renders no tile; the graph-tiles e2e asserts both halves. | . They are collapsible, with the count on the summary so a collapsed list still says how much is behind it — a fixed-height sidebar of tiles must not push the page nav off the top. Theming comes from the avatar’s declared hue: one hue, both schemes derived, so no tile can be legible in one mode and invisible in the other. A per-instance palette would be a second colour vocabulary beside theme.ts.

459815017657.title: On a folio’s own site, a tile describes the FOLIO
459815017657.content: A page’s tiles describe the layer whose site the page is on. A folio’s own Pages site (an IG repository’s folio-site.yml, a document folio’s folio-staging.yml) wears the platform’s chrome, and the platform’s _data/harness.json comes with it: tiles, counts, icon row, rail scopes and title, every path root-relative to the platform’s site. Unscoped, the folio’s badges show the platform’s counts and its links 404. cat-harness-tools/scripts/lib/foreign-site-scope.ts applies the rule to the data, once, for both passes (compose-docs --shell --instance, and rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site): . | the link points at | on a folio’s site it | count | . | the folio’s own root (/<instance>/…) | resolves inside the folio’s baseurl | kept | . | a page the folio’s declaration publishes at its site’s root (/beans/), when the folio IS the checkout’s root (rootOwnPages) | stays root-relative, on the folio’s own site | kept | . | another layer’s state graph (work items, todos, QA, health, uploads …) | is not linked; the icon says why in words | none | . | a platform content, context or derived graph (skills, processes, tools, schemas, docs …) | is re-based, absolute, onto DOCS_SITE_BASE, with its qualifier shown | none | . | a kind nothing classifies | is treated as state | none | . The state row is unlinked rather than shown at zero or re-based. Per schemas/ui/tile-count.ts, absent is a third state, never 0: a folio that declares no beans graph has said nothing about work items. Showing 0 would be a claim, and showing the platform’s number answers the folio’s question with somebody else’s. The icon keeps its place and its accessible name says, for example, *“ declares no beans graph"* (§"An inert row SAYS why"). Ownership is decided by where the link points, never by a kind of the same name. A folio that declares a qa directory does not borrow the platform’s QA tile and its count; borrowing it because the word matched would put the platform’s number back on the folio’s page. A count beside a borrowed link is dropped too: the link is accurate, but the number would still sit on the folio’s page next to the folio’s own. The qualifier is shown instead, so the tile reads as the platform’s. The host’s count projections are not chrome. compose-docs --shell leaves out every assets/**.json that declares a headline tile count, as it does _includes/generated/. A badge whose file 404s renders as ABSENT, with no number. A figure that is not a tile follows the same rule: . | figure | it came from | on a folio’s site it | count | . | the translation sweep badge | _data/translation-qa.json, the platform’s | the shell leaves the file out; the badge stays, inert, reading “QA: not published”, and says why: *“ publishes no translation QA sweep on this site"* | none, and not “not run”, which would be a claim about the folio | . | the navbar’s locale swap | _data/translations.json, the platform’s index of its own pages | the shell leaves the file out; the index reads as null, “could not determine”, and the navbar stays as built | n/a | . | the fsh-guts fish | a button whose count is fetched from this site’s /fsh-guts.json | the button is drawn only when the folio links its OWN fsh-guts; otherwise the fish is the row’s re-based link, named *“the platform’s: declares no fsh-guts graph"*, or an inert icon with the note | none, never ”?”: ? means the read failed | . A folio that publishes its own sweep or fsh-guts document gets its own figure back with no further change: foreignSite.absent (written by scopeHarnessData) only supplies the words for when the site carries nothing. The two _data/ files are named in HOST_DATA_PROJECTIONS, since neither declares what it describes. foreign-site-scope.test.ts fails on a shell that carries a _data/ file nobody has classified as chrome or projection. A folio that IS the root of its own site (for example one whose site is generated rather than a Jekyll tree) needs four more things: . | Its declared pages are its own. Its visualisers under its own site directory publish at the site root, by the same ownsSite || isRepoRoot rule siteDirMount gives its icon (harness-tiles.ts), and the scope keeps them (ForeignScope.ownPages). | The icon row’s own paths and counts resolve on the folio’s site. After scoping, every root-relative href left in the row is the folio’s, and so is the count.json its badge fetches. rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site writes the row’s data-fa-root as the page’s own site root (rowRoot), while its script and style still load from the platform (assetRoot). | Its mark loads from its own site (ownsCheckout). | An image mark can sit on the rail itself. The rail draws the layer’s tone square behind every avatar; a declared image with ground: "none" (KgImageSchema) is drawn with no tone. | . The pinned rail reserves its width. Hover and focus open the bar over the page, as a peek; pinning keeps it open, so .main moves over (docs-ui.css). The gate is foreign-site-scope.test.ts. It runs both foreign-site passes over a folio and asserts (a) no tile carries another layer’s count or links its state graph, (b) no href is left root-relative unless it is the folio’s own path, (c) the platform’s translation sweep and index are not shipped and the rendered head_custom.html hands the badge its words, and (d) the fish fetches no count from a site that has no fsh-guts. The client halves are in translation-badges.e2e.ts and navbar-row.e2e.ts. A check of a page’s chrome has to run on a site that is not the platform’s, because on the platform’s own site the platform’s tiles are right by construction.

d91d69f87c54.title: The glass strip — pinned first, and “+N more” counts the rest
d91d69f87c54.content: No tile may be silently off-screen: a reader cannot tell a tile scrolled out of view from a tile that does not exist. | The pinned set is DECLARED, never written into a surface. glassStrip on the layer’s declaration lists the pins in order: { "chrome": … } for the glass’s own controls (todos, filter, settings) and { "kind": … } for a graph typology. It is inherited along needs like navbarIcons, so absent inherits and [] pins nothing. sync-docs-harness.ts resolves each kind to ONE tile (resolveGlassStrip): the directory named for the kind, else the first glass tile that holds it. A kind several harnesses publish gets one slot, and the others wait in More, where their qualifiers tell them apart. A pinned kind that no tile holds is reported in glassStrip.unmatched and never skipped silently. | Fit, not scroll. The strip shows as many pins as fit at the current width, in declared order, and refits whenever its box changes. It never scrolls sideways (scrollWidth <= clientWidth is asserted at 1280×800 and 390×844). | The last tile says “+N more”, and N is exact. N counts every tile not on screen: pins with no room at this width, plus everything the reader keeps in More. Shown + N is always the total. The tile is a button named “N more tiles”; it opens More and moves focus into it. Pins that did not fit come first in More, marked as pinned. | The reader may still arrange. A strip the reader has arranged, by dragging or with the Strip and More buttons, overrides the declared default in that browser. The fit and the count apply to their arrangement too. | It starts HIDDEN. With no stored choice, the folio opens with the strip slid away. Only its tab shows, reading “Show tiles (N)”. The tab is the one control both ways (board-windows) and carries aria-expanded. The reader’s choice is remembered in this browser as 1 or 0, and storage that cannot be read counts as no choice: hidden. | . glass-strip-fit.e2e.ts holds the four fit assertions and glass-strip-default-hidden.e2e.ts the default.

b25f11792465.title: summary and alsoWritten — what a reader sees, kept apart from why it was named
b25f11792465.content: A harness section on the landing page shows the declaration’s summary, a one-line gloss, and lists alsoWritten, the other spellings of the name. A description made to carry them shows the reader a naming rationale or spellings that render as one line. Authoring notes belong in description or a _comment. The reader-facing line goes in summary, and alternative spellings go in alsoWritten as a list, never inline. A harness’s sticky shows the same text as the landing page. A sticky contribution declares bodyFrom: "summary", and the card’s words are readerText in schemas/content/sticky-contribution.ts: the summary (else the description), then the alsoWritten spellings after “Also written:”. That is the rule docs/_includes/harness_details.html applies, read from the same two declaration fields, so there is no copy of the text to keep in step. bodyFrom: "description" still parses, because the pinned bootstrap/bootstrap.json declares it. bun run cat landing:sticky:check fails when a card built from its declaration does not open with that text. A bodyAppend may follow the reader’s text, and a card with a literal body is not compared.

6c538a5dc35e.title: Asking a person, in one reusable way
6c538a5dc35e.content: Skill human-agent-discussion: Ask a person (or a sibling agent) for what no file holds. First determine where you are — the context, the Role you act as and theirs, the Process and task (or that you are idle) — and ask about whichever you cannot determine before anything else. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question. Named by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Human–agent discussion, Initialize a harness . You are the agent that needs something only a person can supply: a choice, a judgement, or a step only they have the rights to perform. Every diagram in bootstrap that needs one calls processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn as a call activity rather than drawing its own asking.

ad28c4744a9c.title: Before you ask: determine where you are
ad28c4744a9c.content: The diagram’s first three tasks come before any question, and each is declared as a precondition of the first one (bootstrap.processes:precondition … before="A_GiveContext"): . | determine | what you must be able to say | why it comes first | . | the context (A_DetermineContext) | what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs it (the layer’s <name>.json, the diagram you are in, the Skill its task names); and whether the question has already been decided — earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes the person’s ruling | a settled question asked again reopens a decision and spends the person’s attention twice. Cite what you read, not what you remember | . | the Roles (A_DetermineRoles) | which Role you are acting as — the lane of the task that called this discussion — and which Role the person you ask holds | an Actor performs a task in a Process as a Role; nothing is a Role by nature. Who holds the decision decides whom you may ask: only the Requestor chooses a harness | . | the Process and task (A_DetermineProcess) | the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to — “Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent” — or that you are in none: you are idle, classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to | a reader who does not know which Process you are in assumes the last one’s rules still hold | . Say all three in the message, as the first part of the context. A caller that already determined them hands them in; you check them rather than re-derive them. You are out of process — the Process is undetermined — when you cannot name it, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand is not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. What cannot be determined is asked first . When any of the three cannot be determined, that becomes the first question of this same discussion (A_AskUndeterminedFirst), and the caller’s question waits, counted. Ask about the outermost first — the Process, then the Role, then the context — since the outer answer usually settles the inner. It goes through the same order as every question below, and it allows no default: a Process or a Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave you. Its answer is recorded, the three are determined again, and only then is the caller’s question put. If it is declined or met with silence, record what is still open and stop: a step completed in the wrong Process records an authority that was never given. I am in Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, acting as the Bootstrapping Agent. I cannot tell whether you are the person who wants this repository set up, or relaying for someone: the request came from another agent’s message. If you are, I will ask you which harness next; if not, I will stop and record that the Requestor is unknown, since only the Requestor chooses. Are you the person who wants it set up? (One more question after this one.) .

b926b0435606.title: The order is the rule
b926b0435606.content: . | Context. Where you are (the three determinations above), what is being decided, what depends on it, and what you already know, each fact with where it came from. In the message itself: a link is where somebody goes for more, never where the terms are defined. | Options. Every option still open after you narrowed from context, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. An option you could have ruled out yourself wastes the reader’s attention. | Recommendation. The option you would take, marked, and why. | What happens with no answer. Said before the question, so silence has a meaning both sides agreed to before it happened: the default, when the caller allows one, or “the question stays open and the work stops”. | One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. | . The test before you send it: can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, the question is not ready.

ea4629a921ad.title: What can come back, and where each ends
ea4629a921ad.content: | what came back | what you do | end | . | an answer that settles it | record it, and who gave it (a person or an agent) | Answered — or, when it answered a question about where you are, determine again and put the caller’s question | . | an answer that does not settle it (a kind instead of an option; two options) | follow up once, narrower, naming what is still open | back to the answer | . | a refusal | record what was asked and what is still open | Still open | . | nothing | apply the default only if the caller allows one, and say so; otherwise record what is still open | Default applied or Still open | . A default is the caller’s to allow, never yours. A caller allows one only when the decision is reversible and its own instructions name the default. It is recorded as assumed, with the default named, never as the person’s answer, and the next message tells them it was applied so they can reverse it. Which harness a repository becomes allows none: a wrong answer does not fail, it succeeds at being the wrong thing (confirm-harness).

d856a1418f1e.title: The record
d856a1418f1e.content: In the form the caller asks for. For bootstrap’s harness question that is a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json (discussion). For a step only the person can perform (complete-initialization), it is the step with the person’s word beside it. A person saying “done” is recorded as their word, and the next check decides whether it holds.

85ad8c1381d4.title: Symmetric in its participants
85ad8c1381d4.content: The answering lane is a person or a sibling agent that already holds the answer. The record says which, because the two are evidence of different weight. Neither is refused, and they are not conflated.

0f5d62aa9845.title: Human–agent discussion
0f5d62aa9845.content: Process_HumanAgentDiscussion · strict (defaulted) · 13 step(s) . A REUSABLE SUB-PROCESS, never an entry point. Every diagram in bootstrap that needs something only a person can supply — a choice, a judgement, a step only they have the rights to perform — reaches it through a call activity with calledElement=”Process_HumanAgentDiscussion”, rather than drawing its own asking. One way of asking, drawn once: a caller that draws its own has a second answer to “how do I ask”, free to drift from this one. BEFORE ANY QUESTION, THE ASKER DETERMINES WHERE IT IS: the CONTEXT, the ROLES, and the PROCESS and TASK (or that it is idle). Each is a task, declared below as a precondition of the first question. WHAT CANNOT BE DETERMINED IS ASKED FIRST, with no default; the caller’s question waits, counted. THE ORDER IS THE PROCESS: context, then options, then a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then one question. A question the reader cannot answer without opening anything is not ready. A DEFAULT is applied only when the CALLER allows one, and is recorded as assumed, never as the person’s answer. Otherwise silence ends as unsettled. SYMMETRIC IN ITS PARTICIPANTS. The answering lane is a person or a sibling agent that already holds the answer; the record says which, because the two are evidence of different weight. NO work-plan element, and isExecutable is false, for the reasons initialize-harness gives. i i i i i i i i i i i i i

b94822f58c1d.title: How it connects
b94822f58c1d.content: . | Called by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Ask the person | Calls: none | Names the human-agent-discussion skill without calling this process: Determine the harness and repositories — activity-calls-skill-process asks whether each should be a call activity. | Presented on: no docs page section shows this diagram | Skill: human-agent-discussion | Running instances: none recorded | .

91f9926539e6.title: Lanes — who acts
91f9926539e6.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Agent | — | Whichever agent called this sub-process. It determines where it is, prepares the question, rules on whether an answer settles it, and records the outcome in the form its caller asked for. It never supplies the answer itself. | . | Requestor | requestor | The person who asked — or a sibling agent that already holds the answer. Answering, declining and saying nothing are all legitimate moves here, and each has its own end. | .

1c689809e417.title: Steps
1c689809e417.content: Every one of the 13 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Determine the context: what is known, and already decidedA_DetermineContext | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the layer’s <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person’s attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. | . | Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person’sA_DetermineRoles | Agent | human-agent-discussion | An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. | . | Determine the process and task, or that you are idleA_DetermineProcess | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: “Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent”. A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one’s rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the Process, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. | . | Ask first about what could not be determinedA_AskUndeterminedFirst | Agent | human-agent-discussion | The caller’s question waits, and is counted (“one more question after this”). What is put first is the undetermined one: the context you could not establish, the Role you are not sure you hold, or the Process you cannot place this in. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. With more than one undetermined, ask about the outermost first (the Process before the Role before the context), since the outer answer usually settles the inner. | . | Say what is being decided, and why it matters nowA_GiveContext | Agent | human-agent-discussion | First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. A link is where somebody goes for more; it is never where the terms are defined. | . | Lay out the options, with what each costsA_LayOutOptions | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Every option the agent could narrow the question to, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. Narrow from context first: an option the agent could have ruled out itself wastes the reader’s attention. | . | Recommend one, and say what happens with no answerA_Recommend | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Mark the option the agent would take and say why. Then say what happens if nobody answers: the default, when the caller allows one, or that the question stays open and the work stops, when it does not. Said now, so silence has a meaning both sides agreed to before it happened. | . | Ask ONE questionA_PutQuestion | Agent | human-agent-discussion | One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Uses whatever channel the caller is in — in bootstrap, the conversation the person is already in. | . | Answer, decline, or say nothingA_Answer | Requestor | — | The Requestor’s move. Declining is an answer. Saying nothing is not, and is what the recommendation’s “if there is no answer” was for. | . | Follow up, narrowerA_FollowUp | Agent | human-agent-discussion | The answer did not settle it: it named a kind rather than an option, or chose two. Ask once more, narrower, naming what the first answer left open. Once: an agent that keeps asking has stopped narrowing. | . | Record the answer, and who gave itA_RecordAnswer | Agent | human-agent-discussion | In the form the caller asked for — for bootstrap’s harness question, a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json with determinedBy asked. Who answered (a person or an agent) is part of the record. An answer about the context, the Role or the Process is recorded the same way, as the person’s word. | . | Apply the stated default, and say soA_ApplyDefault | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Only the default stated in A_Recommend, only where the caller allows one, and recorded as assumed with the default named — never as the person’s answer. The next message to the person says it was applied, so they can reverse it. | . | Record what is still openA_RecordUnsettled | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Declined, or silent where no default is allowed. The record says what was asked and what is still open, so the next actor resumes rather than restarts. Never a guess. When it is the context, the Role or the Process that is still open, say so and stop: a step completed in the wrong Process records an authority that was never given. | .

23a48e368738.title: Decisions
23a48e368738.content: Every one of the 4 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Context, roles and process all determined?GW_Determined | Judgement. “Determined” means the agent can state each in its message with where it came from; “I think so” about a Process or a Role is not determined. | yes → Say what is being decided, and why it matters nowno → Ask first about what could not be determined | . | What came back?GW_WhatCameBack | Judgement, exercised by the agent — which is why this gateway carries no computed decision. Whether an answer settles the matter is not computable from its text. | settles it → Record the answer, and who gave itunclear → Follow up, narrowerno answer → Did the caller allow a default?declined → Record what is still open | . | Did the caller allow a default?GW_DefaultAllowed | Never for a question about the context, the Role or the Process (A_AskUndeterminedFirst): those allow none. | yes → Apply the stated default, and say sono → Record what is still open | . | Was that the caller’s question, or a precondition?GW_WhichQuestion | An answer to A_AskUndeterminedFirst settles where the agent is, not what the caller needed: determine the three again with it, then put the caller’s question. An answer to the caller’s question ends the discussion. | the caller’s → Answereda precondition: determine again → Determine the context: what is known, and already decided | .

ebc775d2549e.title: Human Translation Workflow
ebc775d2549e.content: Process_HumanTranslation · advisory · 16 step(s) . The human half of translation: a coordinator assigns a locale to a qualified translator, the translator works in their own tool, a subject-matter expert judges accuracy, and only then is the result official. You are in this process when a person is doing the translating. translation-workflow is the machine half — extraction, injection, staleness — and it hands off to this one at exactly the point a judgement is needed. The two are separate because completeness is mechanical and accuracy is not: the coordinator’s gate asks whether enough strings are filled, the reviewer’s asks whether they are right, and no amount of the first substitutes for the second. What makes a translation OFFICIAL is the reviewer’s sign-off, never the file being complete. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

The same lane writes the final status.json once sign-off lands, so the official record sits beside the checks that fed it. | . | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | reviewer | The one reviewer lane in this corpus where sign-off is acceptance: Task_Signoff makes the translation official directly, with no separate editor lane after it, because translation fidelity is the acceptance criterion and there is no different judgement left for an editor to add. | .

For WHO content,the translator should be familiar with WHO SMART Guidelines terminology.The assignment includes:- The .pot file(s) from extraction- The domain glossary- Context notes (block kind, chapter, content area)- The deadline | . | Check translation completenessTask_CheckCompleteness | Translation Coordinator | translation-manager | Verify that all msgid entries have msgstr translations.Partial translations are acceptable for initial submissions but must beflagged for follow-up. The coordinator checks:- % of strings translated- Any fuzzy-flagged entries- Missing critical sections | . | Request completion of remaining stringsTask_RequestMoreWork | Translation Coordinator | translation-manager | Return to the translator with a list of untranslatedor fuzzy strings that need attention. | . | Receive assignment and materialsTask_ReceiveAssignment | Human Translator | translation-managertranslation-managertranslation-manager | The translator receives:- .pot file with source strings (msgid)- Domain glossary with approved term translations- Context notes per string- Style guide and WHO terminology referencesTools: Poedit, Weblate, Crowdin, or direct .po editing. | . | Translate strings in preferred toolTask_TranslateInTool | Human Translator | translation-manager | The translator works through each msgid, producingmsgstr translations. This may happen via:- Git commit + push- Weblate/Crowdin sync- File upload to the coordinator | . | Review translation for accuracyTask_SMEReview | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | translation-managertranslation-managertranslation-manager | A subject-matter expert reviews the injected translatedmarkdown for:- Clinical/technical accuracy of terminology- Preservation of meaning from the source- Cultural appropriateness for the target locale- Consistency with the domain glossaryFor WHO content: the SME verifies that normative statements(“SHALL”, “SHOULD”, “MAY”) are translated with the correctforce in the target language. | . | Return for correction with annotationsTask_ReturnForCorrection | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | translation-manager | The reviewer annotates specific passages that needcorrection and returns to the translator with detailed feedback.Each annotation includes:- The passage in question- What is wrong (terminology, meaning, style)- The suggested correction or reference | . | Sign off translation as officialTask_Signoff | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | translation-manager | The reviewer signs off the translation, making itofficial. This records:- signedOffBy: the reviewer’s identity- signedOffAt: the current timestamp- sourceHash: SHA-256 of the source .md- level: block | section | chapter | folioTool: translation_signoff MCP tool | . | Extract the POTTask_ExtractPOT | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_ExtractPottranslation-manager | Scan the source content and write the translatable strings to .pot files at the configured granularity: segment prose by paragraph, shield what must not be translated (math, code, labels, Lean companions) as placeholders, normalise whitespace, and extract metadata such as titles, alt text and captions. Tool: the translation_extract MCP tool. | . | Prepare domain glossaryTask_PrepareGlossary | Automated Pipeline | translation-manager | Builds the locale term base for the target locale from the layered glossaries, has it reviewed, and hands it to the translator with the POT. Each layer’s glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme’s subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term’s translation; a layer only adds, and may not give a fixed term a second translation. A match in another subject area is a sense check for the reviewer, not a violation. Previous translations of related content are evidence for a term with no fixed form, not a source that overrides one. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme’s catalogue (translation-manager, “The locale term base”). | . | Inject the POTask_InjectPO | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_InjectPotranslation-manager | Read the .po file and the source .md, substitute msgstr for msgid, unshield the placeholders, and write the translated .md to translations/<locale>/. Tool: the translation_inject MCP tool. | . | Round-trip translation QATask_RoundTripQA | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_RoundTripQatranslation-manager | Back-translate the target-language .md into the source language and compare the meaning with the original. It catches semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see, and tells the two apart. Tool: the translation_validate MCP tool.No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, “route drift to a human reviewer”), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. The findings include translation:glossary:check’s: every glossary term translated against the locale term base, fixed before sign-off, with its glossary section in the KG QA report. | . | Append WHO disclaimer (if DAK)Task_AppendDisclaimer | Automated Pipeline | translation-manager | For WHO SMART Guidelines content, automatically appendsthe WHO legal disclaimer:- Translation not created by WHO- English edition is authoritative original- WHO not responsible for translation accuracyOnly applies when folio contentType includes WHO/DAK content. | . | Write status.json (official)Task_WriteStatus | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_WriteTranslationStatus (official = true)translation-manager | Record the translation’s standing in translations/<locale>/status.json. 17d76c54f08f.title: ig-artifact-ingestion
17d76c54f08f.content: Named by: SMART Guideline end to end . Skill id: ig-artifact-ingestion · Package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines · Covers fhir-harness’s fhir-artifact-index graph typology (schema fhir-harness/schemas/fhir-artifact-index.ts). The artefact index of a FHIR Implementation Guide is a knowledge graph keyed by the IG’s own canonical URLs, linking each artefact to its JSON, JSON Schema and JSON-LD representations. No IG publishes such an index itself, so it is always assembled, and it records what each part was built from. This skill says how an index is assembled in this harness; it does not judge whether an IG’s content is correct (that is fhir-validation’s job).

dad8f9312bfb.title: Which IGs carry the IG API overlay
dad8f9312bfb.content: Every IG gets an index; the JSON Schema and JSON-LD links come only from an IG API (WHO calls it the DAK API): the per-artefact sidecars and the enumeration schemas (ValueSets.schema.json, LogicalModels.schema.json) that dak-postprocessing steps 3–6 produce. The index’s sidecarApi says which: . | present — sidecars were found and bound to artefacts; | absent — the source was read and held none; | unknown — nobody looked. unknown is not a kind of absent: only absent is a reason to stop. | . An IG with no IG API is a thin index, not an error.

ca6849160abe.title: Where the index is built: at publish, from the AST
ca6849160abe.content: An IG layer does not commit its fhir-artifact-index/. fhir-harness’s ig-index:build (fhir-harness/scripts/build-ig-indexes.ts) writes it at publish: . | document | schema | built from | . | index.json | folio-fhir-artifact-index/v2 | the IG’s cached AST, by ast-to-artifact-index.ts; its manifest says authority: "cache" | . | menu.json | folio-ig-menu/v1 | the IG’s own sushi-config.yaml menu:, at the commit the checkout’s lock pins (buildMenu) | . | releases.json | ig-releases/v1 | the repository’s GitHub releases, as pointers to their assets; a failed read writes no file, because no list is not an empty list | . | package.tgz | — | the AST’s resources, as package/<Type>-<id>.json, with a package/package.json from sushi-config.yaml | . | sidecars/ | — | the IG API sidecars a layer above writes (ig-site:sidecars), bound to the artefacts | . | contexts/ | — | each .jsonld under input/images/ whose only key is @context | . The IG’s status sits in index.json beside its version, from its own ImplementationGuide. An index that records none has no status this pipeline can state and draws no watermark; that is not “published”. (A separate ig-identity.json once held it and drifted from the IG’s sushi-config; it was excised on 2026-11-14.) . Each document has a different source, so each carries its own provenance. Folding two together would give one file two answers to “where did this come from”. The menu is the IG’s own ordering of itself . sushi-config.yaml’s menu: is a nested map, and order is the file’s order. Never sort it: that would re-navigate somebody else’s IG. Read it from the source config, never from a screenshot: a picture carries no hrefs, and a closed dropdown looks like an empty one. The chrome comes from a chain, and only part of it is the IG’s own . An IG declares its appearance in no file it owns: it comes from the fhir.template chain its ig.ini names, for example . local-template → who.template.root 0.5.0 → fhir.base.template 1.0.0 . So the chrome (folio-ig-chrome/v2) is keyed by the chain’s top template and lives once, in smart-base’s themes/chrome.json, worn by every IG on that chain. It carries layers base-first, and every token records which package won it and what it overrode, which is how to answer whose value is this? For example who.css styles no #publish-box, so the yellow box is HL7’s: the token comes out from: "fhir.base.template" with overrides: []. An overlay is not a merge. --toc-box-border is 1px solid navy in HL7 and navy in WHO — each right in its own layer, but together they make HL7’s rule resolve to border: navy, which is invalid. Every layer parses on its own, so a naive merge ships a broken rule silently. Upstream defects are recorded, never corrected . The chrome mirrors its sources, defects included, and records whose each defect is: . | shape — one token name carrying different kinds of value across layers, as above. | malformed — a value that is not valid CSS on its own terms, such as --breadcrumb-text-color: ##555555 (a doubled # in HL7’s project.css). | . A carried defect shows up in generated pages looking exactly like an ingest bug, which is why the record names its owner. The detector matches one narrow pattern: a false positive would accuse someone else’s stylesheet of a fault it does not have. ingest:ig-chrome:check compares the committed chrome with the template chain. CI cannot fetch the template repositories, so with no source it exits 2 (could not determine), never 0, and it is registered as a report, not a gate. Run it by hand after cloning the IG and its templates.

d3e844627ae2.title: What the AST does not carry
d3e844627ae2.content: . | Category. The Publisher assigns editorial categories when it writes artifacts.html, after the AST is taken. The index uses the Publisher’s default grouping by resource type and names every artefact where a published grouping differs (--keep-published-grouping keeps the grouping of a committed index still on disk). | Where it is published. A canonical URL is an identity, not an address. The published base is the committed copy’s source.of when that names a published site, else the layer declaration’s iriBase, else none, and the run says which. Never derive either the published base or canonicalBase from the other. | . AST-built artefacts are materialized with purpose compiled, and carry the gates of folio-assistant-core/schemas/materialization.ts. sourceLoss and copyright stay unknown until someone establishes them; a permitted there would claim “no restrictions known” without having looked.

a2f2e3183244.title: What is never invented
a2f2e3183244.content: . | canonical is optional. Examples and instance resources have no canonical URL and are most of a large IG. Minting one produces an identifier that resolves to nothing while looking authoritative. | category absent never means “Other”. The IG’s own artefact page has a literal Other section; a second one would make the word mean two things. | A lossy field is left absent, not repaired. An absent field is a fact; a repaired one is a guess. | .

5797eb9afae4.title: When the source is a published site
5797eb9afae4.content: The schema also accepts an index read from a published IG (source.kind gh-pages, output or url), with provenance naming the published file each part came from. These are different evidence: output/ is a local build, gh-pages is what the world can see; never label one as the other. A published IG offers four partial views, none sufficient alone: . | file | holds | misses | . | canonicals.json | canonical URL, version, name | every artefact without a canonical | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | every artefact’s type and id | titles, categories, canonicals | . | artifacts.html | the editorial category and human title (per-row title is ResourceType/id) | anything machine-readable | . | package.manifest.json | package id, version, FHIR version, build date | — | . Traps: . | Read the source, not the page about it. dak-api.html links the enumeration schemas under schemas/, but they sit at the published root. | openapi/openapi.json is not the IG API. On the WHO SMART Trust IG it is the DDCC Gateway API, subject matter that lives there. Key the overlay off each artefact’s own stem (<ResourceType>-<id>.openapi.json), never a directory scan. | .index.json is lossy (Organization entries can carry a truncated "type": "["). canonicals.json is the spine for anything canonical; a field seen only in .index.json stays absent. | .

4c563870891a.title: Running it
4c563870891a.content: bun run cat ig-index:build -- [--only <instance>] [--work <dir>] [--plan] . --plan prints what would be built and touches nothing. Exit 0: every IG found was built; 1: one or more failed (each named); 2: usage. An IG layer is found, with no declaration of its own, when it needs fhir-harness (directly or through a layer above), declares a repository, and that repository carries an AST branch family. A layer missing any of the three is skipped, and the run says which and why. To add an IG, give it those three; never commit or hand-edit the index it produces.

8ab6817d8789.doc: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
8ab6817d8789.title: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
8ab6817d8789.content: Process_IgAstCache · advisory · 6 step(s) . How an IG repository’s own site is published, and how the AST it is built from is kept current (skill ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”). THE RULE. An IG site is built from the IG Publisher AST read from the IG repository’s cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>, never from Publisher HTML. The publish refuses an AST that is not valid for the commit it publishes (ig-cache.sh restore then verify). A later commit that changes no IG input (sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini, input/) does not make the AST stale. THE REFRESH. The cache is written by ONE thing: fhir-harness’s reusable workflow .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml, which an IG repository’s Site publish calls as its first job (ast; template templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml). It runs the Publisher through the AST exporter on a GitHub runner (Java, 10 GB heap, tx.fhir.org). It seeds the branch only from a commit on the default branch whose inputs equal the tip’s. A valid AST is a cache, not a release: every page drawn from it carries the provisional mark (ig-ast-delta). i i i i i i
