53f647a5323b.content: . | Called by: no call activity names this process | Calls: none | Presented on: no docs page section shows this diagram | Running instances: none recorded | .

a2bca0890dce.doc: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
a2bca0890dce.title: Lanes — who acts
a2bca0890dce.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Publication manager (owner, or the agent the owner delegates to) | publication-manager | Starts the AST refresh; an agent never dispatches it on its own (feature-staging §”Agent-run repositories”). When the publish refuses, asks for the refresh rather than publishing around it. | . | Site build (agent, stage-local) | build-pipeline | Restores and judges the AST, builds and publishes the site, then reviews its size against the published one. A stale, cannot-tell or missing AST ends the publish; the size review warns and never refuses. | . | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | ig-publisher-service | fhir-harness’s ig-ast-refresh.yml, run in the IG repository through its caller. Builds the IG once with the Publisher AST exporter and writes the cache branch. Builds no site, publishes nothing, dispatches nothing. | .

43e1bacaf031.doc: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
43e1bacaf031.title: Steps
43e1bacaf031.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Restore and judge the cached ASTTask_Restore | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-ast-deltaig-build-pipeline | ig-cache.sh restore --ig-root . fetches cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> into output-ast/ (with the Publisher’s txcache/), then ig-cache.sh verify runs ig-ast.ts validity: exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (naming which input), 2 cannot-tell. A restore that finds no branch is a miss, judged as not valid. In an IG repository’s site route this is the first pre step, ig-site:ast (ig-repo-site.ts ast). | . | Build and publish the site from the ASTTask_BuildSite | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-render-jekyllig-build-pipeline | Runs the site route’s steps via stage-local.ts → build-instance-site.ts: ig-site:sidecars (IG API sidecars, if the landing layer has the step), ig-site:compose (artefact index and thin pages from the AST, the IG composed at the root), ig-site:openapi (if the IG holds OpenAPI pages), ig-site:publisher-pages (the AST’s resources as <Type>-<id>.json at the root, the build stamp), and last ig-site:bar (the IG’s slim bar on pages written after publisher-pages). Published at the root from the default branch, as a preview otherwise. When the restore recorded the cache commit, the site reads the AST from that commit by raw URL rather than copying it: the artefact pages draw each full resource there, the IG API sidecars are read from its ig-api/ (fhir-harness#344), and the artefact index from its fhir-artifact-index/index.json, which the site points at with fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json instead of serving (#358). The root <Type>-<id>.json copies are then reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data; #359), and the JSON-LD graph (artifact/*.jsonld) names each root file first and the cache copy as its mirror. The full resources are the cache commit’s and the release’s package.tgz. | . | Review the site’s sizeTask_SizeReview | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-publication | Read the size report the build printed before its push, and fix what it shows, or raise a decision card with the owner when no known fix applies (skill ig-publication §”Size review”). The report is cat-harness-tools site-size.ts (bun run cat site:size), written as site-size.json beside the build, never into the site. It gives the total against the published gh-pages root, the top directories, the size by extension, the biggest files, byte-identical duplicates, source maps, the directories named after another layer of index.lock.json, and the directories the shared-assets host could serve. Growth over the budget (10% or 10 MB) is a warning. The review is advisory and never refuses a publish. | . | Dispatch AST refreshTask_Dispatch | Publication manager (owner, or the agent the owner delegates to) | ig-build-pipeline | Actions → “IG AST refresh (by hand)” → Run workflow on the default branch, inputs ref = the default branch, force = false. Set force = true only to rebuild a cache that is valid but suspected wrong. | . | Build the IG with the AST exporterTask_Export | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | ig-publisher-fork | The runner mounts the layers the IG repository’s index.lock.json pins, then restores and judges the cache itself. When it is not valid (or force is set) it rebuilds with the Publisher fork (Tool ig-ast-export, litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher at the pinned claude/ast-export commit). A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller’s optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit’s input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The AST just built must itself be valid for the commit, or the run fails. | . | Seed the cache branchTask_Seed | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | compiled-artefact-cache | ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push: one commit holding the AST, the Publisher’s expansions and txcache/, the IG API generated over that AST (ig-api/, ig-api-cache.ts) and the artefact index built from that tree (fhir-artifact-index/index.json, ig-index-cache.ts), which the site reads by raw URL; its subject recording the package, counts, Publisher version and source commit. Refused when the candidate is under 90% of the incumbent’s resources or edges (the no-shrink gate). | .

655d7879f0a5.doc: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
655d7879f0a5.title: Decisions
655d7879f0a5.content: Every one of the 2 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | AST valid for this commit?GW_Valid | Answered by Task_Restore’s verdict. valid takes yes. stale-inputs, cannot-tell and a miss take no: the publish is refused, never drawn from Publisher HTML or from an AST of other inputs. The override (SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=1, read by ig-site:ast) is for a preview only: on the root it still refuses. | yes → Build and publish the site from the ASTno — refused: stale, cannot tell, miss → Dispatch AST refresh | . | On the default branch, with its inputs?GW_Seedable | Yes when the built commit is an ancestor of the default branch’s tip AND sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and input/ are the same at both. An AST of other inputs never overwrites the shared cache. | yes → Seed the cache branchno → AST kept as a run artifact; cache unchanged | .

b66c1f24f160.title: ig-ast-delta
b66c1f24f160.content: Skill ig-ast-delta: List and view what changed between two IG ASTs, check whether an AST is still valid for the IG’s current inputs, and render the delta as just-the-docs pages that carry the provisional mark. Read before trusting a cached AST, before reviewing an incremental IG build, and before rendering anything from a cache. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, SMART Guideline end to end . Skill id: ig-ast-delta · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness . An instance of the general compiled-artefact-cache pattern; the shared contract is cat-harness’s compiled-artefact-cache skill. The AST’s cache is declared once, as the cache/1.0.0 node caches/fhir-ast.cache.json: its verify is validity below, and its staleness is computed by caches:viz (see ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”). An IG AST is a per-resource dump of what one IG Publisher build held in memory. It is written by the ast-export library, which is built on top of the Publisher rather than inside it (litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher@claude/ast-export, ast-export/). This skill is the consumer half: listing an AST, checking it, diffing two of them, and rendering the result for a reviewer.

ae85f602baac.title: The one rule: a cache, never an authority
ae85f602baac.content: Every AST manifest says "authority": "cache" and lists what is provisional until a full Publisher run: indices, dependency edges and versions. Anything rendered from an AST, or from a delta between two, shows that mark to the reader, on the page itself (ig-publisher-reduction P3). A mark that exists only in a log or a JSON field does not count.

9278bf9585cc.title: Where the files come from
9278bf9585cc.content: | file | written by | says | . | manifest.json (ig-ast/v1) | AstExportCli, AstMerger | every resource with its key, the toolchain, the inputs the AST is valid for, and, on an incremental AST, mixed: true and builtAt per resource | . | dependencies.json (ig-ast-dependencies/v1) | same | every edge, resolved to a resource in this IG or null when the target is elsewhere | . | fsh-index.json | SUSHI (copied by AstExportCli) | the authoritative mapping from source .fsh file to output resource filename, with source line ranges. SUSHI writes it to fsh-generated/data/fsh-index.json; the copy lets a later delta map a file that has since been deleted | . | plan.json (ig-ast-plan/v1) | AstPlanCli | what a delta of changed files means: rebuild, load from cache, remove, or a full build and why | . | delta.json (ig-ast-delta/v1) | ig-ast.ts diff (here) | what changed between two ASTs | . The formats are declared once, and published as JSON Schema . The three ig-ast* formats are declared in Zod in fhir-harness/schemas/ig-ast.ts, and readAst validates through it. The JSON Schemas (draft-07) and a JSON-LD context are generated from that declaration and committed beside it: . | ig-ast.schema.json | ig-ast-dependencies.schema.json | ig-ast-plan.schema.json | ig-ast.context.jsonld | . bun run cat ig-ast:schema regenerates them and ig-ast:schema:check is the CI gate. The Java writer and any downstream consumer validate against these files. Every object is open to fields the writer adds first; authority is the literal "cache", and a manifest claiming anything else is refused. A resource’s key is canonical|version, or Type/id when it has no canonical. Two ASTs are compared by key. An incomplete AST is refused: a missing dependencies.json or a missing or unparsable resource file stops the command, because an empty substitute would diff as “no change”.

a376ed9056dc.title: Commands
a376ed9056dc.content: All of them live in fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts, and each is declared as a Tool: . bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts list <ast> bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts validity <ast> --ig <root> [--toolchain "<ig-publisher X / core Y>"] [--at <rev>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts digest --ig <root> [--at <rev>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts diff <base-ast> <head-ast> [--plan plan.json] [--json delta.json] [--site <dir>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts render <delta.json> --site <dir> bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts jsonld <ast> > ast.jsonld . validity: is this AST still the IG I have? . It reuses folio-assistant-core’s compiledValidity, the staleness check the Lean .olean cache uses. The Java side writes inputs in exactly CompiledInputsSchema’s shape: toolchain, sourceRevision, and inputDigest as 64 hex characters. validity recomputes the digest and the revision from the checkout and compares. | valid (exit 0): built from these inputs. | stale-inputs (exit 1): names which input differs. A changed input/ file is inputDigest; a newer Publisher is toolchain. | cannot-tell (exit 2): never a pass. A manifest without usable inputs, or with a digest in the older sha256:<hex> form, lands here. | . The digest is computed in two languages, Java when writing and TypeScript when checking. A golden vector (58871352384745e1d7fd68f7ea918b0e2febbd86cf36a9cb5f0c7ce9d13a82f1) is asserted by both test suites. If you change the algorithm, change it and the vector in both places; a drift makes every AST read as stale, or a stale one read as valid. A later commit that changes no input is the same source. If the recorded sourceRevision is an ancestor of HEAD and the recomputed inputDigest equals the recorded one, the revision counts as unchanged (sameSourceAs), so a README merge does not make the cache stale. A recorded commit the checkout cannot see (a shallow clone, another branch) stays stale. After a build, check the commit, not the work tree: --at <rev>. The Publisher writes under input/ during a build: it renders input/images-source/*.plantuml into input/images/*.svg, overwriting tracked files and adding untracked ones, so a work-tree digest taken after the build is not the commit’s and a freshly built AST fails its own check. validity --at HEAD (and digest --at HEAD) hashes the inputs as committed (inputDigestAt); in a clean checkout this equals the work-tree digest and the exporter’s. ig-ast-refresh.yml instead restores input/ with git before its check. The toolchain cannot be read from a checkout. Without --toolchain it is assumed unchanged, and the result’s current says so. When the Publisher you would run is known, pass it. diff: list what changed . Resources are added, removed, changed or versionChanged. A version move (same canonical, different version) is paired, not reported as a removal plus an addition. Each changed resource carries a differential: JSON paths whose value was added, removed or changed, capped at 200 rows per resource, with the overflow counted rather than dropped. Edges are listed as added or removed. --plan folds the incremental plan’s decision in. The differential is structural, over the dumped JSON, not FHIR-semantic: reordering a repeating element shows as a change at every index, and a narrative regenerated with a new timestamp shows as a change. Read it as “these bytes moved”, and judge meaning yourself. render: view it in the pipeline . --site <dir> writes just-the-docs pages: index.md (the list, grouped by resource type, with counts, the plan, and edge changes) and one page per changed or version-changed resource (path, op, base, head). | Every page opens with the provisional mark. Do not remove it to make a page look finished. | Liquid in values is neutralised, not merely wrapped. FHIR narratives carry Liquid output and tag delimiters (double braces, brace-percent). A raw block around the page is not enough: a value containing the raw block’s own closing tag would end it. So every value gets a word joiner (U+2060) inside each opening and closing delimiter; the text reads the same, and Jekyll parses nothing. This skill names those delimiters in words because its own reference page is rendered inside a raw block by gen-skill-docs; do not write the closing tag literally here. | One page per key, not per Type/id. Page names carry a hash of the key, as the AST’s own files do, so two versions of one resource are two pages. | Table cells escape |, which a key contains (canonical|version). | . Put the pages under the IG’s own just-the-docs site (see ig-render-jekyll) as a child section, so the reviewer keeps the site’s navigation.

2ce239030a5b.title: Where this sits in a process
2ce239030a5b.content: The review is drawn as its own subprocess, fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn. In fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn it belongs between Task_Merge (restored and rebuilt records merged) and Task_Qa (QC gates on the aggregate), which that diagram does not yet show: it is what the QC reviewer reads to decide whether the incremental result is what a full build would have produced. The steps, in order: . | validity on the base AST. stale-inputs or cannot-tell means no incremental build; run a full one. | AstPlanCli for the delta of changed files. The planner uses two maps: . | Forward (fsh-index.json, from SUSHI): which .fsh file produces which FHIR resource. This is the authoritative answer. | Reverse (fsh-file-users/v1, from fsh-cone --file-users): which files depend on a given file. This is how a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file (which produces no resource itself) reaches the resources it affects. | . | IncrementalBuildCli (or a full build, if the plan says so). | diff base head --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/. | The reviewer reads the rendered delta. A difference they cannot explain is a missed coupling in the cone rules, not a curiosity: file it as a work item and run a full build. | .

256b03891d69.title: Which rendered pages a source change reaches
256b03891d69.content: Before any build, fhir-harness/scripts/ig-rendered-impact.ts predicts the rendered files a change to .fsh, .cql or input/pagecontent alters, through fsh-cone and SUSHI’s fsh-index.json, as a rendered-impact/v1 (skill rendered-impact in cat-harness). An AST diff afterwards confirms it: a resource the delta reports changed whose page the prediction did not name is a cone defect. bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-rendered-impact.ts --ig <root> --base origin/main --head HEAD [--ast <output-ast>] --out impact.json .

fc654e2664f4.title: Do not
fc654e2664f4.content: . | Do not treat a clean validity as a correct AST. It says the AST was built from these inputs, not that the build was right. | Do not diff a merged (mixed: true) AST against a full build and call every difference a bug. Check builtAt first. A resource carried from the base was not rebuilt, and the difference may be the change itself. | Do not render from an AST whose validity you did not check. | Do not re-implement any of this in a CI workflow. CI calls these same scripts and tools, so a CI result and a local result are the same measurement.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml (ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”) does exactly that: ig-cache.sh, ig-ast.ts validity and AstExportCli. | .

fc6ea355562f.title: ig-binary-artefacts
fc6ea355562f.content: Skill ig-binary-artefacts: Where the IG Publisher’s binary outputs go — full-ig.zip, package.tgz and its R4/R4B variants, package.db, validator packs, and the definitions, examples and expansions zips — and why a pages branch is the wrong place for them. Measure a branch with ig-binary-audit before deciding anything. Read before configuring an IG’s deploy or release step, before linking a download from a page, and before a pages branch grows past its size limit. Named by: An IG release: the owner tags, a draft is built, the owner publishes . Skill id: ig-binary-artefacts · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness · Tool ig-binary-audit .

a5e99ec3d913.title: What the Publisher writes
a5e99ec3d913.content: Besides its pages, an IG Publisher run writes about twenty binary files into output/. PUBLISHER_BINARIES in fhir-harness/scripts/ig-binary-audit.ts is the list, not this paragraph. They fall into three groups: . | The package. package.tgz (with package.r4.tgz, package.r4b.tgz and sometimes package-combined.tgz) is what a FHIR tool installs. It is the one binary a consumer cannot do without. | Derived bundles. full-ig.zip (the whole site), package.db, validator.pack and validator-<id>.pack, ai.zip, and the definitions, examples and expansions zips in JSON, XML and Turtle. Each is recomputable from the package or the build. | Spreadsheets. csvs.zip, excels.zip, schematrons.zip, and spreadsheets.zip where a script bundles the loose .xlsx files. | .

724f77ac703f.title: Why a pages branch is the wrong place
724f77ac703f.content: A pages deploy copies output/ as it is. Each branch preview is another full copy, and git keeps every byte for good. GitHub Pages publishes at most 1 GB; on one measured IG gh-pages branch, 966.5 MB were Publisher binaries and 94 % of those were copies in 29 branch previews (full-ig.zip alone: 30 copies, 644.7 MB). Deleting files over 100 MB before deploy removes none of these, because each copy is under the limit.

2bdd99607197.title: Where each one goes
2bdd99607197.content: . | A preview carries no binaries. A reviewer reads pages, and binaries are published only on releases. | A release carries the package and whatever the IG promises to distribute. Upload them as release assets, and link the release from the downloads page. The link names the repository it is built in, never a hard-coded upstream. | The knowledge graph points at release assets and does not hold them. fhir-artifact-index/releases.json (ig-releases/v1) records each asset’s name, size, digest and download URL. Anyone who wants the bytes fetches them from there. ingest-ig-releases (Tool of the same name) writes it from GitHub’s release list. | The IG’s just-the-docs site lists them on a generated releases page (fhir-harness/scripts/templates/ig-site/releases.liquid): file, size and SHA-256 per release, each linking to the asset. | The published IG’s root may keep package.tgz, since FHIR tooling fetches <canonical>/package.tgz. Nothing else needs to be there. | What this pipeline renders from the package reads it from the served knowledge graph, never from a pages branch. The resource JSON views fetch the package.tgz that ig-index:build writes into fhir-artifact-index/ at publish. | Each resource is at the site root as <Type>-<id>.json, reduced. FHIR readers expect the Publisher’s names beside the pages, so the site serves every resource of the AST there (fhir-harness#359), but not whole: minified, with no text narrative, and each Library ELM attachment (contentType naming elm) without its data, pointing by url at the full resource in the AST cache. The CQL is a link too: url at the IG’s .cql source, or else the full resource. On one measured IG that is 13 MB instead of 47 MB. The full resources are the AST cache commit’s (by raw URL, which the pages read) and the release’s package.tgz and ast-data.zip. SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 turns the root copies off (ig-build-pipeline §”What the site serves from the AST”). | .

c370f495f9e1.title: Releasing
c370f495f9e1.content: The owner set this process on 2026-11-09 (Q-REL-1 “A”). A release is cut from a tag, carries the same files every time, and is published by a person. The process is ig-release.bpmn. | The owner tags the IG’s current version. Releasing is a governance decision: the owner tags the commit that set the version in sushi-config.yaml with v<version> (for example v0.2.0) on the default branch, and pushes the tag. An agent never chooses a version, never pushes a tag and never publishes a release; it reports what is missing (below) and stops. | The tag starts the build. Pushing the tag runs the IG’s ig-release.yml caller (template: templates/ig-repo-site/ig-release.yml). It can also be started by hand for an existing tag. | The build is full. The caller runs ig-ast-refresh.yml with force and release set. A release is never cut from an incremental AST. | Every release carries the same files. ig-release.ts assets gathers them: . | package.tgz, plus package.r4.tgz and package.r4b.tgz when the build wrote them; | ast-data.zip, the IG’s AST, whose Library resources keep their ELM; | SHA256SUMS. | . The Pages site serves neither the AST nor the ELM: its root <Type>-<id>.json copies are reduced (rule 7), and the ELM ships here. A build with no package.tgz is refused. | It is made as a GitHub draft. ig-release.ts draft makes the draft and uploads the files. If the tag already has a draft, its files are replaced. If the tag already has a published release, it is refused, because a published release is never changed by a workflow. | The owner publishes it. Publishing the draft on GitHub is Task_AuthorizeRelease in draft-to-publication.bpmn. Until then nobody but the repository’s writers sees it, and ingest-ig-releases leaves it out of releases.json. | A ballot, draft or CI-build version is a pre-release. ig-release.ts kind reads sushi-config.yaml: . | a version with a pre-release suffix (1.0.0-ballot) is a pre-release; | so is a releaseLabel naming a ballot, draft, CI build, preview or snapshot; | anything else, including STU1 and trial-use, is a release. | . Pre-releases are recorded in releases.json with their flag, and the site’s releases page lists them. | . A ci-build version the owner tags is released as a pre-release; one the owner does not tag gets no release, and its Pages site is the preview. Catching up a version that was not tagged . Every AST refresh of the default branch runs ig-release.ts check (advisory: it never fails the run, never tags and never releases). It reads the version in sushi-config.yaml and prints a notice for what is missing: . | version X is untagged: the owner tags commit <sha> with vX. The commit is the one that last set the version (git log -G over sushi-config.yaml), not necessarily HEAD; when the history cannot say (a shallow clone), HEAD is named and the notice says so. | tag vX has no release: run "IG release (draft)" (ig-release.yml) by hand with tag vX, for a tag pushed before the IG carried the caller or whose run failed. | vX has a draft release waiting for the owner to publish it. | . To run it by hand: bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-release.ts check --ig . --repo <owner/repo> (a draft is listed only to a token that may write the repository). An older version left untagged is not reported: only the current one is a release the owner may still want.

da926b5ea0cb.title: Measure before deciding
da926b5ea0cb.content: git fetch --depth 1 origin +refs/heads/gh-pages:refs/remotes/origin/gh-pages bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-binary-audit.ts --repo <checkout> [--ref origin/gh-pages] [--json] . It reads the git tree, not a checkout, so a multi-gigabyte branch costs a depth-1 fetch and no disk. --previews <prefix> changes where previews live (default branches/).

c7ca45b3fcf3.title: Do not
c7ca45b3fcf3.content: . | Promise a download the release does not carry. A downloads page that lists assets no release has is a reader sent to a 404. Check the list against the release’s actual assets, not against the script that was meant to upload them. | Treat “under 100 MB” as fine. The limit that matters is the branch, and the copies add up. | Delete binaries from a published pages branch on your own initiative. Report the measurement and wait to be told (deletion-requires-confirmation). | .

aa1d638fd7aa.title: ig-build-pipeline
aa1d638fd7aa.content: Skill ig-build-pipeline: The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs . Skill id: ig-build-pipeline · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness . The base: run the FHIR IG Publisher over an IG, with no pre-processing and no post-processing, and publish the result. It serves any FHIR IG; see §”What this layer refuses to know about”.

f2173813c6f6.title: The pipeline
f2173813c6f6.content: input/fsh/ → SUSHI → fsh-generated/resources/ input/pagecontent/ ┐ sushi-config.yaml ┘ → IG Publisher (JVM, Docker) → output/ → publish to a pages branch . The publish target (the pages branch) is declared by the layer. SUSHI and the Publisher both need packages.fhir.org. Where it is refused, see fhir-validation §”When a package host refuses you” before concluding either cannot run.

a1a7aea99758.title: Source of truth versus compiled, cached and rendered output
a1a7aea99758.content: The boundary is declared in schemas/ig-content-type.ts: contentTypes.ig.include in index.config.json defaults to ["input/**", "sushi-config.yaml", "ig.ini", "publication-request.json"] and excludes output/**, temp/**, template/**, fsh-generated/** and input-cache/**. Only the files inside contentTypes.ig.include (plus any declared ig-annex directory) are hand-authored source. | Authoritative source (edit here) | Compiled, cached or rendered output (never hand-edit; overwritten on build or publish) | Basis | . | sushi-config.yaml (id, canonical, version, status, releaseLabel, fhirVersion, dependencies, pages, menu), ig.ini, publication-request.json | fsh-generated/resources/ImplementationGuide-*.json, output/, fhir-artifact-index/menu.json, fhir-artifact-index/releases.json, site.data.fhir | schemas/ig-content-type.ts (IG_DEFAULT_INCLUDE), ig-render-jekyll | . | input/fsh/**/*.fsh | fsh-generated/resources/*.json, fsh-generated/data/fsh-index.json, fsh-generated/includes/fsh-link-references.md (even when fsh-generated/ is committed in a legacy checkout, it is SUSHI’s compiler output — edit the .fsh source, never the generated JSON) | schemas/ig-content-type.ts (IG_DEFAULT_EXCLUDE), ig-ast-delta §”fsh-index.json” | . | input/cql/**/*.cql and input/maps/**/*.fml | Compiled Library (base64 ELM/CQL content[]) and StructureMap resources in output/ and output-ast/ | l3-fhir-authoring, ig-ast-delta | . | input/pagecontent/**/*.md, input/includes/**, input/translations/**/*.po, and declared ig-annex directories (annexes.json) | Rendered HTML in output/, composed thin pages in $SITE_WORK/ / docs/, and copied assets/annex/* | ig-render-jekyll §”Thin pages, the default”; §”The IG repository’s site route” below | . | input/images-source/*.plantuml | input/images/*.svg written by the Publisher when a same-stem .plantuml exists in input/images-source/ (hand-placed static assets under input/images/ with no .plantuml stem are source) | ig-ast-delta §”validity” | . | input/** + sushi-config.yaml + ig.ini | output-ast/ and the AST cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> (manifest.json with "authority": "cache", dependencies.json, fsh-index.json, expansions.json, txcache/), written only by ig-ast-refresh.yml | §”The AST cache lifecycle”, ig-ast-delta | . | The AST + sushi-config.yaml | fhir-artifact-index/ (index.json, menu.json, releases.json, sidecars/), <Type>-<id>.json, artifact/<Type>-<id>.{html,jsonld,json}, assets/ig-search.json, folio-build.json, and the published site on gh-pages (root and branches/<branch>/) | §”The IG repository’s site route” | . An overlay using pre-export or ig-site:sidecars documents its own authority table in its own skill. This layer puts back everything pre-export touched before it records the clean commit’s input digest (§”The AST cache lifecycle”).

5da296856b89.title: Version numbering: SEMVER for a FHIR IG
5da296856b89.content: An IG’s version is declared in sushi-config.yaml version (and mirrored in publication-request.json version when cutting a release). It is always an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semantic version triple (versionIncrement: "major" | "minor" | "patch" in ig-publication; directory-conventions §”Pinning a reference”), never a range or floating tag. Which segment bumps is determined by the delta on the IG’s published conformance and canonical surface since the previous release — measured over the AST with ig-ast.ts diff <prev-ast> <next-ast> (ig-ast-delta §”Diffing two ASTs”), not from commit messages: . | Increment | What triggers the bump on a FHIR IG | Examples | . | major (X+1.0.0) | Any breaking change to the IG’s canonical conformance surface, terminology bindings, CQL/operation signatures or FHIR version that can invalidate a conforming instance or downstream dependent IG | Removing or renaming a canonical resource (StructureDefinition, ValueSet, CodeSystem, Library, PlanDefinition, Measure, Questionnaire, OperationDefinition, ConceptMap, StructureMap); tightening cardinality (0..* → 1..*, 0..1 → 1..1) or adding a new required (min >= 1) element or error-severity invariant on an existing profile or logical model; strengthening a binding to required or replacing its bound ValueSet incompatibly; removing or changing the meaning of a concept in a published CodeSystem; incompatible change to a CQL library’s public expression names/types or an OperationDefinition’s parameters; changing fhirVersion; or a breaking major bump in dependencies: | . | minor (X.Y+1.0) | Any backward-compatible addition to the IG’s canonical resources, profiles, terminology, logic or narrative structure | Adding a new canonical resource (profile, logical model, extension, ValueSet, CodeSystem, ConceptMap, Library, PlanDefinition, Measure, Questionnaire, ActivityDefinition, ActorDefinition, Requirements); adding an optional (min = 0) element, optional slice or warning/guideline-severity invariant to a profile or logical model; adding concepts to a CodeSystem or widening a ValueSet expansion (extensible / preferred / example bindings); adding examples/instances or new narrative pages in sushi-config.yaml pages:; or a compatible minor update in dependencies: | . | patch (X.Y.Z+1) | Any backward-compatible fix that adds no canonical resource and breaks no conforming instance | Narrative prose, layout or typo fixes in input/pagecontent/**; description, title, comment or mapping metadata edits on existing elements; translation updates in input/translations/**; fixing invalid example instances; bug fixes in CQL expressions or FML maps that preserve declared inputs, outputs and clinical/functional intent; or rendering/theme fixes | . Release vs development cycle and dependency pinning: . | Cutting a release (vX.Y.Z): requires human release-authorization (ig-publication), a full AST build (ig-ast.ts build-kind output-ast --require-full), status: active and releaseLabel: release in sushi-config.yaml, a matching version: "X.Y.Z" entry in publication-request.json, and every entry under sushi-config.yaml dependencies: pinned to an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release version — never current, dev, a branch name or a commit SHA (checked by bun run cat check:published-refs). | Between releases on the default branch: sushi-config.yaml carries status: draft and releaseLabel: ci-build (or ballot during a ballot cycle) with the next target MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version. Pre-release ballot or candidate cuts may append -ballot or -rc.N while keeping the target MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH core. | Overlay co-versioning: when an overlay pairs the IG with an upstream domain model in index.config.json contentTypes, the overlay’s own skill defines how the two version numbers relate. | .

6f7e240f0cb6.title: What the site build emits: thin pages, by default
6f7e240f0cb6.content: The Jekyll phase emits thin pages: each artefact page and the IG’s artifacts.html and toc.html are a few KB that load their content from JSON-LD nodes (artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld and artifact/index.jsonld). Each artefact’s tab views (definitions, mappings, JSON and examples) are thin pages beside it, drawn from the resource’s JSON. The IG’s narrative pages keep their prose, with every piece of chrome linked rather than inlined. Full pages: pass --full-pages to gen-ig-pages.ts and stage-ig-sites.ts. What each page holds, and the QA over the nodes, is ig-render-jekyll §”Thin pages, the default”.

a5761ae8d79b.title: The AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST
a5761ae8d79b.content: Process: ig-ast-cache.bpmn. The declared cache. The cache branch is the cache/1.0.0 node caches/fhir-ast.cache.json (cache-first CI, rule 6), and ig-ast-cache.bpmn is its component of the harness’s one optional cache process: Task_Restore and GW_Valid are the component’s verify, and Task_Seed is its save. The dispatched AST refresh (Task_Dispatch, Task_Export, on the Java runner) stays this cache’s own save path. The node carries the key recipe (ig-ast.ts digest), the producer, the consumers, the save policy and the uses. The stored key against the key today’s inputs imply, and so whether the cache is stale, is computed by cat-harness-tools’ caches:viz, never written here. Only a step that builds or renders an IG restores it (owner, 2026-11-05: “not all rendering/CI/merge processes need all caches. be optimal”). A test shard, a gate or a merge job never does. The incremental build (process ig-incremental-build, opt-in fhir-harness.collab) does not restore the AST itself: its Task_Restore calls the harness’s cache process, Process_Cache (cat-harness, skill cache-first-ci), whose plan restores the layers ref and then this cache for an IG target. That process draws this cache as a task in its own lane, since a layer below this one cannot call into it; ig-ast-cache.bpmn stays the component’s steps. The node’s materializes (output-ast/, input-cache/txcache/) is how a plan decides that: a target needs this cache when what it reads touches those paths. Its needs is layers-ref, so the layers are restored first. Every restore, verify and refresh prints one line in cached-step’s format, **cached-step ig-ast: hit|warm|miss** (exact) — <why>. Key `.` (`ig-ast.ts cache-line`). `warm` means the refresh applied a delta over an older AST. The key is the input digest: it is derived from the content of the inputs, so a merge or rebase that leaves them alone keeps it. Terms: . | AST: the per-resource dump the IG Publisher AST exporter writes (output-ast/; formats in ig-ast-delta). | Cache branch: cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> on the IG’s own repository. Its tip holds the AST, the Publisher’s expansions.json and its txcache/; each seed is a child of the previous tip, so every commit a site was built from stays reachable for pages that read the AST by raw URL pinned to that commit (owner, 2026-11-10; fhir-harness#325). <package id> is sushi-config.yaml’s id. | Valid: ig-ast.ts validity says the AST was built from the inputs the commit being published has (Publisher version, sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini, input/). | . The rule. | The site is built from the cache-branch AST; the publish runs no Publisher and never uses the Publisher’s HTML. Its first step is ig-site:ast (ig-repo-site.ts ast): ig-cache.sh restore --ig-root ., then validity, as ig-cache.sh verify does. §”The IG repository’s site route” has the steps after it. | The publish refuses an AST that is not valid: stale-inputs, cannot-tell, or no cache at all. It does not fall back to a Publisher build or to the Publisher’s HTML. A preview (a STAGING, non-release build) accepts a stale or cannot-tell AST by default (owner, 2026-11-05: “preview/staging (non release) builds can be on stale cache”): publish it at once, never wait on a cache refresh for it. SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0 makes a preview refuse one too. The root still refuses; folio-build.json records the verdict the preview was built on. | A commit that changes no input does not make the AST stale. If the recorded commit is an ancestor of HEAD and the input digest is unchanged, the AST is still valid (sameSourceAs in ig-ast.ts), so a README or workflow merge needs no rebuild. A checkout that cannot see the recorded commit (a shallow clone) reads as stale. It never reads as valid. | Only a Publisher run refreshes the cache. Whenever the IG’s source changes, someone has to run it. The workflow below is the usual writer. When its run is queued and the root has to go out, build it where the checkout is (owner, 2026-11-05: “local/agentic build and push to gh-pages”): bash fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast-build.sh --ig-root . (the workflow’s build step as a script; it needs Java, Maven, Node, Ruby and the Publisher’s network; pass the same --template-repo the caller gives the workflow as template-repos, e.g. --template-repo who.template.root=WorldHealthOrganization/smart-ig-template for a WHO IG, whose #current template the build server does not list), then bash fhir-harness/scripts/ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push on the default branch, then the publish. Do not wait on a queued runner for a publish an agent can do. | . Who writes the cache: one workflow, here.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml (workflow_call) is the only writer. The IG repository calls it from templates/ig-repo-site/ig-ast-refresh.yml, copied unchanged, which runs on a push to the default branch that changes the IG’s inputs or that file, and by hand. The repository’s site-publish.yml (the template) does not seed the cache: it waits for this commit’s refresh, because the IG publisher declares after: ["ig-ast-refresh.yml"] (scripts/ig-publisher.ts; cat-harness-tools site-publish-after.ts), and then restores the cache. The push that adds the caller runs it, so a repository’s first publish has an AST; when the cache branch is still missing, ig-site:ast refuses and says to dispatch the refresh once. One run: . | mounts the layers the IG repository’s index.lock.json pins; | restores and judges the cache for ref (default main); | if the cache is not valid, or force is set, runs the caller’s pre-export command when it gives one, then builds the IG with AstExportCli (Tool ig-ast-export, pinned ast-export-ref). The exporter comes from its published bundle, the release ast-export-<commit> that ast-export-bundle.yml builds once per pinned commit, when its sha256 matches scripts/ast-export-bundles.tsv, and is built from source otherwise. The bundle, the pinned Jekyll gems and the FHIR packages are kept in the fhir-ig-tooling cache; | puts back what pre-export changed in the inputs, and checks that the new AST is valid for its own commit; | seeds the cache with ig-cache.sh seed --push, only when the commit is on the default branch with the tip’s inputs. Otherwise the AST is uploaded as a run artefact, output-ast. | . A stale cache is rebuilt incrementally; a release is cut from a full build. Step 3 does not always run a full Publisher build: . | When the cache is stale, the run is not force, and the caller gives no pre-export, it runs IncrementalBuildCli over the restored cache. That rebuilds only the cone of what changed and merges it over the cache (skill ig-publisher-fork). Its own plan falls back to a full build when it cannot tell, and a failure, or a merged AST that is not valid, falls back to AstExportCli. | A cache that is missing or cannot-tell, a force run, and a caller with a pre-export always build in full. A pre-export changes the work tree, which the incremental build refuses. | The run’s kind output, and ig-ast.ts build-kind output-ast, say which kind of build it was: full, or incremental (the manifest is mixed, with an incremental lineage). | A release is cut from a full build only. Any step that cuts a release runs ig-ast.ts build-kind output-ast --require-full, which exits 1 on an incremental AST. To get a full AST, run the refresh with force. | The site says which kind of build it came from. folio-build.json carries ast.kind beside ast.verdict (ig-repo-site.ts, the publisher-pages step). | . A preview is built from its own branch’s AST. The template’s ast job passes ref: github.ref_name, and when that run rebuilt without seeding, the publish job downloads the run’s output-ast before ig-site:ast runs, which keeps an AST already in the checkout when it is valid for the commit. So a branch that changes the IG’s inputs gets a preview of its own content, and the shared cache stays the default branch’s. folio-build.json names the AST it used (ast.commit, ast.verdict) beside source. Seeding is refused below 90% of the incumbent’s resources or edges (the no-shrink gate in compiled-artefact-cache). The run builds no site, writes no gh-pages and dispatches nothing. The Tool node is ig-ast-refresh. An overlay’s preparation: pre-export. Some IGs prepare their inputs before the Publisher runs: an overlay registers pages in sushi-config.yaml or generates resources from other sources. The caller passes the command as the optional pre-export input, written in its own workflow file. This layer runs it with bash at the IG root and knows nothing about what it does: the overlay names its own steps. The run records the clean source digest (ig-ast.ts digest) before pre-export, restores the inputs after the export, checks the digest again, and writes it into the manifest’s inputs (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The prepared tree’s digest and the command go under preExport, so the cache verifies on any clean checkout. A failing pre-export fails the run, and nothing is seeded. When it runs. Only when a person, or an agent named for that run, dispatches it. An agent never dispatches it on its own (feature-staging §”Agent-run repositories”). Adding a push trigger on the default branch, filtered to sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and input/**, is decided per repository by its owner.

fe8875235984.title: What this layer reads: contentTypes.ig.include
fe8875235984.content: An IG repository declares which paths this layer reads in its root index.config.json; nothing else is read: . "contentTypes": { "ig": { "include": ["sushi-config.yaml", "ig.ini", "input/fsh/", "input/pagecontent/"] } } . The section is the ig content type (schemas/ig-content-type.ts). An entry ending in / is a directory and covers everything under it; any other entry is one file. Paths are repository-relative and POSIX: absolute paths, .., ., backslashes and empty segments are refused. sushi-config.yaml is not the marker: a repository is an IG source because it declares the section. Every IG reader here honours it. Each one asks scripts/ig-read-scope.ts (igReadScope(root)) before it touches a path: build-ig-indexes, ig-repo-site, build-ig-site, fsh-cone, ingest-ig-menu, ig-api-hub, ig-site-data, ig-review-data, measure-logic-layer-edges and check-translation-supplements. An undeclared optional directory (input/images/, say) reads as absent; an undeclared file a reader cannot work without (sushi-config.yaml) is refused with the path named. ig-repo-site compose and stageIgSite stage from a copy of the declared paths only. Not gated: index.config.json itself, and the ig-ast.ts input digest, which must match the Java exporter’s. The list bounds the harness, not SUSHI or the Publisher. A repository that declares no section is a legacy IG. Every path is read, and each run prints one warning per repository: . warning: <root> declares no contentTypes.ig in its index.config.json, so fhir-harness reads it as a legacy IG (every path). Declare "contentTypes": { "ig": { "include": [...] } } there, listing the paths the harness reads (see fhir-harness schemas/ig-content-type.ts). When you see it, declare the section; do not silence the warning. A section that is there but has no include, an empty one, or a bad entry is refused outright: a section that declares nothing is never read as “everything”. Adding a path. When a page, a diagram or a data file is missing from the site and the IG declares the section, check include before the reader. Add the path to contentTypes.ig.include in the IG’s own index.config.json (a directory with a trailing /), in the same pull request as the content that needs it, and say in the description which reader needed it. Add the narrowest path that covers it, never "" or the repository root. Example: the WHO SMART Base IG includes input/diagrams/, input/archimate/, input/dmn/ and input/ignoreWarnings.txt.

73ba139b27d6.title: The IG repository’s site route: the layers supply the steps
73ba139b27d6.content: An IG repository declares no site.build. It holds index.config.json with "site": {"landing": "<layer>"}, and the site route (stage-local.ts, cat-harness-tools) asks the mounted layers’ script table for these step names, never naming a layer: . | slot | when | provided by | what | . | ig-site:ast | pre, required | this layer | restore the AST from the cache branch and judge it (rule 1 and 2) | . | ig-site:sidecars | pre, optional | the landing layer | the IG API sidecars from the AST, into $SITE_WORK/ig-api/ | . | render:bpmn | pre, optional | cat-harness-tools | the site’s drawing of every diagram, at docs/assets/img/workflows/ of the harness’s docs, which the process pages embed; built at publish, never committed | . | ig-site:compose | source, required | this layer | the artefact index from the AST, the thin pages, the IG composed at the root | . | ig-site:openapi | site, when the IG holds openapi/cat-openapi.config.json | cat-harness-tools | a page and an IRI for each OpenAPI operation, at openapi/ | . | ig-site:publisher-pages | site, required | this layer | the AST’s data served, the Publisher-chrome guard, the build stamp | . | ig-site:bar | final | this layer | the language picker and the IG’s slim bar on the pages the platform wrote after publisher-pages (ig-repo-site.ts bar); and it leaves out another IG layer’s served artefact index that the platform’s mount copied in (dropForeignIndexes; owner, 2026-11-10: another layer’s content is cross-referenced, not copied — that IG publishes its index on its own site) | . The handshake with a layer above (ig-repo-site.ts): . | Input: a sidecar step leaves its files in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/sidecars/. | Descriptor: what the IG calls them, in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/ig-api.json ({ "label": "..." }). | Binding: this layer binds whatever is there to the artefacts by the Publisher’s file names (ast-to-artifact-index.ts --sidecars), labels the pages with the descriptor’s label, and serves the files at fhir-artifact-index/sidecars/. It knows no producer and writes no label down; with nothing there it binds nothing and the pages say “IG API”. | Serving path: files the layer above leaves in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/site/ (its own pages over the sidecars, such as an OpenAPI page at openapi/index.html) are served verbatim at the site root, never over a path the site already holds. The Publisher-chrome guard judges them like every other page. | Placeholder exception: a page of the IG’s own that holds the descriptor’s "placeholder" marker is a shell around the layer’s content, and the layer’s page at the same path replaces it. No other page is replaced. | In the AST cache commit (owner, 2026-11-10, card “A”): ig-cache.sh seed runs the same step over the AST it seeds (ig-api-cache.ts) and commits its ig-api/ (sidecars/, site/, ig-api.json) beside the AST, so the generator’s flags stay the layer above’s. When ast recorded the cache commit and the restored AST holds ig-api/, the site binds that copy instead and copies none of it: the index records sidecarBase (<raw>/ig-api/sidecars), every API tab, view page, hub entry and OpenAPI embed reads <sidecarBase>/<file>, the hub’s documents are <raw>/ig-api/site/<file>, and only the site’s pages over them (the Swagger page) are served. An older cache with no ig-api/ falls back to the step’s output in the work directory, served as above. | The artefact index, too (owner, 2026-11-10, card “A”): the seed also commits fhir-artifact-index/index.json, built from the tree it commits (ig-index-cache.ts: compose’s flags, every localPath a path in that tree, the sidecars at ig-api/sidecars/, no sidecarBase). When the restored AST holds it, the site does not publish the index; it serves fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json (fhir-artifact-index-ref/v1): index is the raw URL of the cache copy and base the commit’s tree, which its paths resolve against. An older cache: the site serves its own index.json, and the pointer says "index": "index.json". A reader on another site finds the index with locateArtefactIndex(<site>): the pointer, else the old path. The pages themselves read their index at build time; no page fetches it. ast-history.json stays on the site: it is written at build time from the commits behind the one restored. | The Swagger page lists each spec at the address it is read from: ../fhir-artifact-index/sidecars/<file>, or its raw URL (rebaseSwaggerSpecs); the generator’s ../<file> named a root path where no sidecar is served. | . What the site serves from the AST: each resource once, under the Publisher’s name <Type>-<id>.json at the root, as FHIR’s convention and the IG Publisher have it (owner, 2026-11-10, card “C”; fhir-harness#359; no ast-data/ mirror, owner 2026-11-08); the artefact index, or the pointer to the cache’s copy (above); and the AST as site.data for the IG’s own pages. When ast recorded the cache commit, the pages read each resource IN FULL by raw URL at that commit, and the root copy is reduced (ig-repo-site.ts reduceForSite): minified, without text (the pages render the narrative from the full copy), and each Library attachment whose contentType names elm without its data, its url set to the full resource in the cache; the CQL likewise becomes a url (the IG’s .cql source, or else the full resource). Measured on one IG of 756 resources: 47 MB verbatim, 13 MB reduced. The JSON-LD graph names the root file first (each node’s local encoding, each artifact/index.jsonld entry’s schema:contentUrl) and the cache copy second (mirror); ig-artifact-jsonld.ts check holds every local file to the built site. The full copy is the cache commit’s and the release’s package.tgz (ig-binary-artefacts). The root name is read from the resource (resourceType, id), not the cache file’s name; two names that differ only by case are warned about, as they clash on a case-insensitive disk for the Publisher too. SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 serves no root copy when the pages read by URL; without a cache commit (or with SITE_AST_BY_URL=0) the root copy is the pages’ own and is served whole. The grouping of the IG’s committed fhir-artifact-index/index.json is kept when it holds one, since the AST stops before the Publisher assigns categories. Annexes an IG’s pages load on demand (a data dictionary, say, rather than the full workbook): . | What an annex directory is: the one directory an IG repository declares for this layer, because the data is the IG’s own and no AST holds it. It is of the generic ig-annex kind (typologies/ig-annex.json) and holds annexes.json (ig-annexes/v1: { page, file, columns? } per annex, file beside it). The files themselves sit in a directory nested inside, declared with the producing layer’s own kind; this layer names none of them. | Who reads it: compose and stage-ig-sites.ts, through annexesFor. Each copies every file to assets/annex/ and mounts ig-annex.js on the page. An index also reads a committed fhir-artifact-index/annexes.json if present (legacy location; do not use). | Link check: a .md annex is appended to its page as written, so its links address that page, not the directory holding the file. The kind says so (shownOnPublishedPages), which keeps them out of the harness’s source-tree link sweep, and bun run cat check:ig-annex-links (scripts/check-ig-annex-links.ts) judges them from the host page instead: each x.html must be a page the IG serves, and each #id an id that page (its annexes included) carries. | .

0c4bf2085db7.title: The deploy phase
0c4bf2085db7.content: Deploying to a pages branch belongs to this layer: the history page, the CI build banner, the release-link fix, deleting files over 100 MB, and a deploy that retries on a ref conflict. Commenting on a pull request that a deploy finished belongs to cat-harness. Every build also prints a size review before its push: the site against the published one, and what weighs most. It is advisory and never refuses. What to look at and the usual fixes are in ig-publication §”Size review”; the step is Task_SizeReview of ig-ast-cache.bpmn.

80dfe012cdc9.title: Who starts a build
80dfe012cdc9.content: Before an adopted IG repository publishes on its own, two questions are put to its owner: whether automatic gh-pages builds become manual-only, and whether to install the just-the-docs site. They are in fhir-ig-create §”4. Who starts a build”.

159bd33fb677.title: What this layer refuses to know about
159bd33fb677.content: A list, because “generic” is a claim and a list is checkable. fhir-harness must contain no reference to: . | dak.config.json (dak.json as upstream still spells it), the DAK logical model, or any DAK component | smart.who.int canonicals, or any WHO publisher metadata | the DAK API’s NAMES and its PRODUCTION — the label “DAK API”, the dak-api.html hub page and its DAK_API_* markers, and the post-processing that writes the sidecars. Rendering the sidecars an IG publishes is generic and IS here, as the IG API (ig-api-views.ts). A WHO layer passes its names in as configuration (--sidecar-label, --api-hub-page, --api-hub-markers, --api-placeholder); nothing here writes them down. The per-artefact .schema.json, .displays.json and .openapi.json sidecars are that API, not DAK’s. | the DAK pre- and post-processing steps, in either direction | anything in the authoring-who-smart-guidelines package | . The WHO package may reference this layer; this layer may not reference the WHO package. A violation fails no build on its own: the layer simply stops being usable for a non-WHO IG. Gate: bun run cat check:fhir-harness-exclusions (in smart-base). A mention is not a dependency. Comments, markdown, and JSON _comment or description values are counted and never graded. Code (string literals included), other JSON values, and BPMN outside <documentation> are graded. The DAK step names are read from the WHO layer’s own pre/post-processing tables, so this list does not restate them. It is a ratchet: existing hits are in a committed baseline, each with a reason. A new hit fails, and so does a cleared one the baseline still allows, until --shrink lowers it. Never widen the baseline to admit a hit: move the WHO-specific part up, or have the WHO layer pass it in as a parameter (the IG page generator’s --sidecar-label is that shape already).

49e8232abb4d.title: Translation supplements: compiled on every pull request
49e8232abb4d.content: An IG’s translated FHIR terms are CodeSystem supplements, one FSH file per locale in input/fsh/translations/<locale>.fsh. The IG build compiles them, but it is often not run on a pull request, so an IG repository copies templates/ig-repo-site/translation-supplements.yml into .github/workflows/ unchanged. Its one job is . uses: litlfred/fhir-harness/.github/workflows/translation-supplements.yml@main . which runs scripts/check-translation-supplements.ts (Tool check-translation-supplements). It compiles the IG’s CodeSystem, Alias and RuleSet entities with every translation file in a throw-away FSHOnly SUSHI project, requires 0 SUSHI errors, and checks that each supplement supplements a CodeSystem of this IG, designates only that CodeSystem’s codes, has the file’s locale as its language (and no designation in another), and that no CodeSystem id is used twice. An IG with no input/fsh/translations/ passes as not applicable. It reads only sushi-config.yaml and input/fsh/ within the IG’s include. Nothing is resolved at run time. SUSHI is the version scripts/ig-toolchain.env pins (SUSHI_VERSION; no IG’s sushi-config.yaml names one), installed from scripts/sushi/package-lock.json with npm ci --ignore-scripts; the check refuses a lockfile or binary of another version, and a test fails when the lockfile and ig-toolchain.env disagree, so a SUSHI bump changes both in one pull request. The FHIR core package for the IG’s fhirVersion is pinned by sha512 in scripts/sushi/fhir-packages.lock.json and fetched from the npm mirror; a fhirVersion it does not list is refused. SUSHI runs with a package cache made for the run and no network, and the run fails if anything but the pinned core package appears in that cache.

7e7559353315.title: Generic post-processing scripts
7e7559353315.content: strip_library_binaries.py and strip_library_content.py strip base64 payloads and inline CQL/ELM out of Library resources. Nothing in either is DAK-shaped: any IG depending on hl7.fhir.uv.cql produces oversized Library resources. They live in scripts/library-strip/ (byte-identical copies, with upstream commit, licence and hashes recorded, and a test that runs them on a non-WHO IG’s output). Three more generic transforms live here: generate_logical_model_schemas.py (a JSON Schema per logical model), generate_valueset_schemas.py (a JSON Schema per ValueSet, plus the enumeration-response schemas) and generate_jsonld_vocabularies.py (JSON-LD from ValueSet expansions). The test for this layer: a step that reshapes what the Publisher already emitted belongs here. A step that adds a constraint, a profile or a WHO-specific name stays in the overlay. The per-artefact API sidecars and their hub are the FHIR IG API above; only their DAK label stays in the overlay. The Tools are declared in fhir-harness/tools/.

ebf1490771fb.title: Upgrading to the overlay
ebf1490771fb.content: An IG that wants the DAK surface does not change this pipeline; the WHO harness above it (the WHO SMART Base IG, whose DAK document kind carries the pre/post steps) supplies them as an overlay. The base takes no position on whether an overlay exists, and must not gain a flag for one — a do_dak input at this layer would be this layer knowing about DAKs.

4352c1e1d51e.title: Version floating is real here
4352c1e1d51e.content: publisher.jar is re-downloaded from the latest release on every WHO build, so two builds of an unchanged commit can differ. If this layer pins instead, say so in the layer’s declaration and make the pin visible in the QA record.

ee470ccd52d4.title: ig-build-pipeline (skill)
ee470ccd52d4.content: The skill ig-build-pipeline as its source file fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

244bb5fac201.doc: Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs
244bb5fac201.title: Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs
244bb5fac201.content: Process_IgDocsSiteCompose · advisory · 4 step(s) . How a host docs site builds every IG it mounts INSIDE itself, so each IG’s pages wear the host’s chrome (one sidebar, one search, one language selector) rather than being a site of their own. NO IG PUBLISHER RUNS. build-ig-site turns the IG’s source into Jekyll source, with the Publisher’s site.data.fhir filled from the IG’s AST and sushi-config.yaml, and the host’s ONE Jekyll build renders it with just-the-docs (skill ig-render-jekyll). Which IGs is DATA: each instance whose fhir-artifact-index/menu.json records a source.of (the IG repository) and source.ref (the commit). No workflow and no step here names an IG. feature-staging.yml runs the same steps for a pull request’s preview, with --changed-files, so only the IGs a change reaches are rebuilt. aa327fbf5d89.title: ig-publication
aa327fbf5d89.content: Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, An IG release: the owner tags, a draft is built, the owner publishes . Skill id: ig-publication · Package: fhir-ig-authoring · Named by activities in l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn (Build pipeline and Publication manager lanes), ig-incremental-build.bpmn (Incremental build, Publisher + validator services (JVM) and Publication manager lanes), ig-ast-cache.bpmn (Site build lane, the size review) and ig-release.bpmn (the owner’s tag). Build a FHIR Implementation Guide and publish it: version, tag, assemble the site, deploy. Sourcing. The IG Publisher and the FHIR publication process are HL7’s; an IG’s own publisher sets its release conventions. This skill states how publication is wired in this harness — which lanes, which authority, which binaries — and defers to those for what a published IG must contain.

edae9a58270e.title: Inputs and outputs
edae9a58270e.content: fhir-harness/schemas/skills/ig-publication/: . | in — igRoot (required), versionIncrement (required), releaseNotes, publicationTarget | out — version (required), publishedUrl (required), releaseTag, releaseBranch, publicationRequestPath, buildStatus | . How versionIncrement ("major" | "minor" | "patch") is chosen from the AST delta against the previous release, and which files in igRoot are authoritative source versus compiled, cached or rendered output, is defined in ig-build-pipeline §”Source of truth versus compiled, cached and rendered output” and §”Version numbering: SEMVER for a FHIR IG”.

3ae07a5f69dd.title: Authorising a release is not the same as managing one
3ae07a5f69dd.content: Two permissions, two holders: . | permission | held by | means | . | release-authorization | programme-manager, admin | may decide a release happens | . | release-management | publication-manager | may configure, build, version and deploy one that has been authorised | . draft-to-publication.bpmn marks Task_AuthorizeRelease and Task_PublishRelease relaxable="false": no package’s workflow-policy.json may relax either, with or without a reason. An agent never records the authorisation. skills/requirements/agent-workflow.json states it as a SHALL: an agent shall not record an approval, a sign-off or a decision to release on a human’s behalf. Building the artefact is this skill’s job; deciding it ships is not.

2092169df3b7.title: The toolchain
2092169df3b7.content: java -jar "${IG_PUBLISHER_JAR}" # default /opt/ig-publisher/publisher.jar jekyll build # site assembly . ig-publisher is a declared capability of this package and requires java-runtime; jekyll is not one of its declared capabilities.

a40619cce0f1.title: What the Publisher run produces
a40619cce0f1.content: The Publisher is one step in an IG’s build. An overlay may wrap it in pre- and post-processing of its own, which that overlay’s skills describe; this layer names none of them. The run itself produces: . | it produces | notes | . | output/ — the rendered site | HTML per resource and per page, from input/pagecontent/ and sushi-config.yaml’s pages: | . | {ResourceType}-{id}.json per resource | the structured surface everything downstream reads | . | .xml and .ttl per resource | not read, rendered or linked by this platform — see the JSON-only contract in ig-render-jekyll | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | filename / resourceType / id, index-version 2 | . | canonicals.json, package.manifest.json | partial views of the same artefact set | . | artifacts.html | the only source of an artefact’s category | . | qa.json | the validation record, uploaded as a workflow artifact | . | POT files | extracted translatable strings | . It also does two things no post-processing step can. It validates every resource against its profiles and the declared FHIR version, and it resolves the dependency closure (hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.uv.cql, hl7.fhir.uv.cpg, hl7.fhir.uv.crmi, hl7.fhir.uv.sdc for a clinical-reasoning IG) with version pinning and terminology expansion against tx. A cache cannot fake that resolution, which is why the phased transition keeps the Publisher for the AST and QA. Where it is invoked from . Inside Docker (hl7fhir/ig-publisher-base), with publisher.jar downloaded from the latest release on every run. The toolchain version is therefore not pinned: two builds of an unchanged commit can differ.

553206da674e.title: Full build versus restored state
553206da674e.content: ig-incremental-build.bpmn restores derived state and assembles the site without a full publisher run, fast enough for an authoring loop. A release is cut only from the full publisher build in that same diagram, in the JVM services lane. Never publish from restored state: the site looks right and was never built by the publisher the release claims produced it.

54b3a48a41f0.title: Cutting a release
54b3a48a41f0.content: A release starts from a v* tag, never from a site deploy, and the tag is the owner’s: releasing is a governance decision (ig-release.bpmn, Task_Tag). The owner tags the commit that set the current version in sushi-config.yaml with v<version>; an agent never picks a version or pushes a tag. Pushing the tag runs the IG’s ig-release.yml (template templates/ig-repo-site/ig-release.yml): a full AST build, then ig-release.ts makes a GitHub draft release carrying package.tgz (and its R4/R4B variants), ast-data.zip and SHA256SUMS. Publishing the draft is the owner’s Task_AuthorizeRelease; a workflow never changes a published release. The files, the pre-release rule and the order are ig-binary-artefacts §”Releasing”. The site itself is published from the AST cache (ig-ast-cache.bpmn) and carries none of these files. Catch-up. Every AST refresh of the default branch runs ig-release.ts check, which reports, as a notice, a current version with no tag (naming the commit to tag) or a tag with no release (run “IG release (draft)” by hand for it). Relay the notice to the owner; do not act on it. The details are ig-binary-artefacts §”Catching up a version that was not tagged”.

adc2ab5577bd.title: Report the URL only once it answers
adc2ab5577bd.content: publishedUrl is a measurement. A deploy that has returned is not a site that serves — GitHub Pages takes minutes on a first publish. Probe it, and until it answers report not-yet or unknown, never a live URL. scripts/pages-bootstrap.ts implements this three-state probe and decisions/pages-live-gate.dmn states the same logic as a table.

573a2e093065.title: Pages of statements extracted from the IG’s sources
573a2e093065.content: When the IG draws on library sources, the statements extracted from them are published as pages of the IG before the Publisher runs, each linked to its library entry and section. That is core’s standard step (publish-extracted-statements, bun run cat statements:pages), the same for every content type. What the IG supplies is its look, and nothing else: . | the page spec’s out is a page under the IG’s own page content directory, so the Publisher and the site route render it like any other page; | its tableAttr is the kramdown class the IG’s tables use (for example {:.grid}); | the page is registered in the IG’s own sushi-config.yaml pages and menu. | . statements:pages --check runs in the IG’s CI, so a page that no longer matches its extraction fails the build.

9d5639313659.title: Size review
9d5639313659.content: Owner, 2026-11-10: “add size review as part of authoring process”. An IG’s Pages site had reached 216 MB and was brought back to about 25 MB by hand. The review exists so that it does not grow back. It is a step of every publish (ig-ast-cache.bpmn, Task_SizeReview, after Task_BuildSite). It is advisory: it warns and never refuses a publish, unless the owner later rules otherwise. What runs. Every local or preview build through stage-local.ts / build-instance-site.ts prints the size report (cat-harness-tools site-size.ts). It writes site-size.json beside the build (in <repo>/../<instance>-site/, next to _site/), never into the published site. To run it by hand: . bun run cat site:size --site <build>/_site --lock index.lock.json \ --against-ref origin/gh-pages --repo . # git fetch origin gh-pages first . The build compares with the published root when the build has read it (a root build’s parity guard). Otherwise it compares with the local origin/gh-pages (git ls-tree -r -l, which reads no blobs), and failing that, with the last site-size.json. The previews (branches/, STAGING/), _render-log/ and PC/ are not counted as the site. What to look at, in this order: . | The total and the comparison line. A ⚠ the site grew line means the build is more than 10% or 10 MB over the published site (--budget-pct, --budget-mb). Find which top-level directory and which extension account for the growth. | Directories named after another layer. The instance list comes from index.lock.json. Another layer’s pages, artefact index or assets in this site are a copy. | Byte-identical files. The same bytes published under several names: one index as .json and .jsonld, a resource beside its .source.json, a script under two paths. | Source maps. Any .map file. | Shareable directories. Directories the shared-assets host could serve, but the site still carries. | The biggest files and the extension table, for whatever is left: a bundle, a schema, a database, an image set. | . The usual culprits, and their fixes: . | culprit | fix | . | vendored libraries (form renderers, the Form Builder, WebAssembly builds, editor bundles, harness images) | serve them once from the shared-assets host the IG names in index.config.json site.sharedAssets (cat-harness-tools lib/shared-assets.ts); a directory the host does not serve yet stays local, and the build says so | . | another layer’s pages, index or assets | link that layer’s own site rather than copy it (the scoped site’s relinking; ig-site:bar leaves out another IG layer’s artefact index); the owner’s ruling is that another layer’s content is cross-referenced, not copied | . | AST resources, sidecars or the artefact index mirrored onto the site | point at the raw URL of the file at the AST cache commit (§”The AST cache lifecycle” of ig-build-pipeline): the pages read each full resource there, the sidecars from its ig-api/, the index through fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json. Each resource is served once at the root as a REDUCED <Type>-<id>.json (no narrative, no ELM data: 13 MB instead of 47 MB on one measured IG); SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 drops them | . | source maps | not published: strip .map files and their sourceMappingURL comments at build | . | several indexes of the same artefacts (index.json, index.jsonld, a search index, a menu) | one index, from which the others are derived in the browser or left out | . | Publisher binaries (full-ig.zip, package.tgz variants, validator packs) | release assets, not pages-branch files (ig-binary-artefacts) | . When to raise a card with the owner. Raise a decision card when the growth warning holds and none of the fixes above applies. Raise one also when the fix would drop content a reader uses, or when it needs a parity ruling (the published root carries something this build would no longer carry). Put the comparison line, the top three contributing directories and the proposed fix on the card. The review stays advisory, so a preview may still publish while the card is open. Do not widen the budget to silence the warning.
