6346252b7eb8.title: Skills it satisfies
6346252b7eb8.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. dcf99ee20156.content: write turns an artefact index into artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld under a docs root, with no .json twin: one folio-ig-artifact-jsonld/v1 node per artefact, in borrowed vocabularies only (the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org, PROV), naming the artefact’s canonical URL, its representations and, for a compiled copy, what built it. With --root-resources (the IG site’s default) the first representation is the reduced <Type>-<id>.json the site serves at its root (local), the second the full copy in the AST cache by raw URL (mirror), and each index entry names the root file (schema:contentUrl). check is the kind’s QA: over a BUILT site, every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node is its own file’s, no .json twin is served beside it, and every local resource it names is on the site. It also writes and checks the index node, artifact/index.jsonld (folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1): every artefact once, each entry naming its node. 9563ae9773ff.title: Skills it satisfies
9563ae9773ff.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. a34ec217a0d7.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. fb2ade1e0430.title: Skills it satisfies
fb2ade1e0430.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. 31c3853f76ea.title: Build an IG repository’s own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration
31c3853f76ea.content: The three checkout scripts the platform’s site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG’s cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG’s input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves each of the AST’s resources once, as <Type>-<id>.json at the root (no ast-data/ mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 — the artefact index (or fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json, pointing at the cache’s copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher’s chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES, so the site build reports the IG’s own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them. |   |   | . | Tool | ig-repo-site | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/fhir-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | fhir-harness | . | source | fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site/ig-repo-site.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

a2660e564fed.title: Skills it satisfies
a2660e564fed.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. ae02a8938e11.title: Build each IG instance’s artefact index from the IG’s cached AST

b3691895684b.title: Skills it satisfies
b3691895684b.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. Also satisfied by: build-ig-site, fhir-core, ig-artifact-jsonld, ig-ast-refresh, ig-page-render-qa, ig-pages, ig-publisher-i18n, ig-repo-site, ig-site-data, ingest-ig-menu, jsonld-vocabularies, logical-model-schemas, stage-ig-sites, strip-library-binaries, strip-library-content, terminology-index, valueset-schemas. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/ig-build-pipeline/{input,output}.schema.json).

55ec73f930ea.title: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
55ec73f930ea.content: Lay down each declared remote mount — a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json, or, in a folio with no index, a remoteMounts entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, index.lock.json (a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root .gitignore block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through writeDeclaredMounts into index.config.json. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts, rule H8): a person’s consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. --staging mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or mountDefaults names may be one the layer declares in its <name>.json or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (skills/skills.json naming voices), resolved at the pin through instanceDirectories; an id in neither is refused at plan time. tools on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts), its implementation (the inProcess.module, or the script its bun run cat <key> resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools’ importClosure (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A hydrated mount lays each chosen directory down as its published index.hydrated.jsonld only: read from the pin’s git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin’s subgraph index package (the subgraph-index-<sha> release asset subgraph-index-package publishes), its tarball checked against its folio-binary-release/v1 record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, SubgraphHydratedSchema and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package’s URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. --check compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. e3af20d1aac8.title: Package one pin’s subgraph index files for a hydrated mount
e3af20d1aac8.content: Pack every built index.jsonld and index.hydrated.jsonld under a layer’s <docs>/subgraph/<harness>/ into ONE npm package for one pin — <harness>-subgraph-index@0.0.0-pin.<sha>, with a folio-subgraph-index/v1 manifest giving each file’s sha256 — through pack-tarball (bun pm pack), which also writes the tarball’s folio-binary-release/v1 record. The reusable workflow layer-publish-subgraph-index.yml attaches both to the GitHub release subgraph-index-<sha>, where remote-mount finds them for a hydrated source whose pin’s git tree holds no index file (they are builtAtPublish, so none does). It builds nothing: run subgraph:jsonld first. No subgraph files under the layer is a refusal, never an empty package. |   |   | . | Tool | subgraph-index-package | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/subgraph-index-package.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/subgraph-index-package/subgraph-index-package.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

822175a990a8.title: Check that an ArchiMate model’s fhir-actor tags point at the IG’s FHIR ActorDefinitions
822175a990a8.content: Actors come first: the IG’s ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK’s personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a #person actor on an application or technology element, a #system actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; --strict makes that a failure. --json prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-actors | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors/archimate-actors.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

dc9c665adcd4.title: Skills it satisfies
dc9c665adcd4.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. 9f59d501db93.title: Skills it satisfies
9f59d501db93.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. 7b3ec24fd549.title: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
7b3ec24fd549.content: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness’s declaration at its pin and every needs, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless –repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch’s tip unless –pin says otherwise, its declaration’s name checked), seeds them all into the repository’s index.config.json with the consent given (remote-mount --seed --whole), sets site.landing to the harness, site.agentRun and mountApprovers, mounts the closure (remote-mount: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (.github/cat.ts and .github/mount-from-lock.sh from cat-harness-tools templates/root-bootstrap/) and sets the root’s cat script to bun .github/cat.ts, so bun run cat … mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness’s instantiate:<harness> checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches// (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin =` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of =<owner/repo>` says where a need lives. |   |   | . | Tool | instantiate-harness | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness/instantiate-harness.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

14a66ba369e1.title: Skills it satisfies
14a66ba369e1.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: folio-init. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, kg-retrieve-npm, mount-from-lock, npm, subgraph-index-package. a23de4ef6237.title: Every reference a journey or a workshop names resolves
a23de4ef6237.content: Read every user-scenario and workshop node in the checkout through the layers’ declared directories, with the journeys viewer’s own resolver, and resolve what each names: actors (personas, a step’s lead, experiences[].actor, handoff.from/to, illustrationStyle.cast[].actor), user stories, realisedBy BPMN files (instance-relative) and the element ids in them, uses blocks in a directory declaring building-blocks, req: requirements, FHIR examples and a step’s dak assets (data sets, decision tables, indicators) in a fhir-artifact-index (could not determine while the index is built at publish), illustration.src files, follows/partOf/parts/includes journeys (parts and includes forming no cycle; an includes held against the call activity its step’s realisedBy names, could not determine when the call names no process), the trustLadder code list and each record.state code of it, and ArchiMate views; and each workshop’s scenarios, steps[] {scenario, step} and <scenario>#<step> refs; each device screen’s owner and personCard actors, its steps[] {scenario, step}, and the FHIR examples its qr and recordList blocks name; and every persona’s avatar image path. Every journey is a DAK user scenario (the kind specialises it): its DAK personas, the roles its persona actors play, must be non-empty and each a declared role; a persona may be an actor or (0.4.0) a role. What is derived is not also written: a listed part’s follows or partOf, personas equal to the parts’, a lead equal to the lanes’ first actor, are each a redundant finding, and a 0.4.0 step with no experiences whose lanes no persona plays is a finding. A node that does not parse is a finding. One line per finding, naming the layer, file and step. fc0b107d7e8a.title: A package’s exports are its declared, shipped code directories

db3a08400cfb.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: mount-from-lock, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. 82df6697bee4.title: Skills it satisfies
82df6697bee4.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, running, superseded (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or --out could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. --markdown and --warn always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither. | string · Markdown text. 9a12a4464567.title: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
9a12a4464567.content: Before a model reads a sub-agent’s report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are control (steers what the receiver does) or data (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator’s plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. Exit 0 clean, 1 refused, 3 quarantined, 2 could not determine. |   |   | . | Tool | handover-screen | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/handover-screen.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/handover-screen/handover-screen.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

da46939b4843.title: Skills it satisfies
da46939b4843.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. sub-kg-lifecycle . A sub-KG is a knowledge graph staged as a directory inside a harnessed repository, declared as its own layer, that may later leave for a repository of its own. The lifecycle: declare it in place, grow it, stage it for separation (one import seam, the separation guard, a self-contained rehearsal), and then, each behind an explicit owner confirmation, create the repository, copy the staged contents in with history, re-point the declaration, verify on a fresh clone and delete the in-repo copy. The light sibling of kg-separation: use this for a DATA layer that leaves whole, and kg-separation when a graph must split into a content repository and a tools repository. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/sub-kg-lifecycle.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/sub-kg-lifecycle/{input,output}.schema.json).

68a191531357.title: Collect candidate translations from open engines
68a191531357.content: Ask one or more open, self-hosted machine translators — OPUS-MT (Helsinki-NLP Marian models, CC-BY 4.0, run locally) and/or a self-hosted LibreTranslate (AGPL, Argos models) — for CANDIDATE translations of each empty or fuzzy string, so no freemium API quota is involved. Candidates are appended to <locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json (translation-candidates/v1) for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page; a candidate whose placeholders or markup do not round-trip is not recorded. Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation: an EMPTY msgstr gets the first good candidate, marked #, fuzzy; a non-empty msgstr is never overwritten. The translation node records the source (generatedBy: "machine", model, time); official is never set, and a candidate is never a verdict. A catalogue that says DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, or whose node is official, gets candidates but no fill. |   |   | . | Tool | translation-candidates | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/translation-candidates.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/translation-candidates/translation-candidates.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

6b964f2a59bc.title: Skills it satisfies
6b964f2a59bc.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-refresh . The translation watcher: a scheduled fresh session that keeps every locale of every layer current after the source moves. Cold start, then, per layer, detect, refresh the templates, merge them into each locale, translate only the new and fuzzy strings with the fixed terms, run the gates, round-trip the changed strings, write the QA report, open one PR to main, merge it only where the layer declares merge-when-green, and report source mistakes as one issue. Use for “refresh the translations”, “a template check failed”, and when scheduling or running the watcher. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-refresh.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-refresh/{input,output}.schema.json). translation-candidate-source . The one interface every candidate-translation engine meets: for a layer’s catalogues, append candidate translations per string to the translation-candidates/v1 sidecar, each carrying its source, and seed an empty msgstr with the first candidate marked fuzzy. An agent model and the open machine-translation engines (OPUS-MT, LibreTranslate / Argos) are interchangeable behind it. Use when adding an engine, choosing one, or producing candidates for review. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-candidate-source.md. Also satisfied by: translation-candidates-agent, translation-platforms. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-candidate-source/{input,output}.schema.json).

1c8d81685430.title: Publish a built site to gh-pages as a full replace
1c8d81685430.content: Lay a built _site onto a gh-pages checkout as a FULL REPLACE and push it, keeping the open pull requests’ staging previews: each attempt re-reads the branch, re-runs restore-staging and keep-shared-payloads against what is on it now, replaces the tree, commits docs(gh-pages): site from <sha> and pushes. A rejected push is rebuilt, never rebased (a rebase would re-apply the replace over a preview a sibling just deployed), up to three attempts. A restore that cannot read the branch stops the publish. A site that matches the branch is a no-op, not a failure. It publishes and does not verify: the workflow’s verify step runs after it. |   |   | . | Tool | publish-gh-pages | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/publish-gh-pages.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/publish-gh-pages/publish-gh-pages.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

067507b03a95.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-adjudication.md. Also satisfied by: github, translation-adjudication-workflow, translation-review-page, translation-status-viewer. eafb552bb90d.title: Publish a folio’s or an IG’s site from the agent’s own checkout — the one agent publish path
eafb552bb90d.content: Build a repository’s site in the agent’s checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared site.build recipe (built by build-instance-site), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — folio-staging.yml for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG’s ghbuild.yml for a FHIR IG, whose build job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (sync-docs-harness, then rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>): every page gains the rail and the icon row #fa-navbar-row, and the IG’s own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose index.html wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; --plan stops there, --dry-run composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, --artifact writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead. |   |   | . | Tool | stage-local | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/stage-local.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/stage-local/stage-local.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

ba1bfc298391.title: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer’s own site, or a branches/ preview
ba1bfc298391.content: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer’s own gates (--pre), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (/<repo>, or /<repo>/branches/<branch> for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. It never decides to publish: only --publish does, and then a root publish keeps branches/ and _render-log/ on the branch, and a preview replaces only its own branches/<branch>/. |   |   | . | Tool | build-instance-site | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/build-instance-site.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/build-instance-site/build-instance-site.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

394eb35d7593.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs
394eb35d7593.content: Rewrite every third-party uses: owner/repo@ref outside the declared staging-only workflows to @<full commit SHA> # <ref>, so Dependabot keeps the pair current. A tag resolves to its PEELED commit (an annotated tag’s object is never pinned), else a branch head, by git ls-remote with argv. A ref that resolves to nothing, or to more than one commit, is refused and reported, never guessed. This repository’s own reusable workflows are first-party and left alone. 36ab5b48cf77.title: Skills it satisfies
36ab5b48cf77.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-manager . Translation lifecycle management for folio content. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, the poSources fallback resolution chain, and translating into several locales as a team: one extraction, a PR per locale to main, FHIR terms as CodeSystem supplements, the untainted round trip as run, and the per-locale QA report. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-manager.md. Also satisfied by: translation-extract, translation-inject, translation-platforms, translation-roundtrip-record, translation-status, translation-validate, translation-qa-prune. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-manager/{input,output}.schema.json). decision-audit . Record why a decision was made, or why a finding in it was left. Required of whoever adjudicates a gate, and of the agent that assembles the citations for them. Every overrule of a mechanical finding carries a note, and every note cites corpus evidence. Source: cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/decision-audit.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/decision-audit/{input,output}.schema.json).

The check every BPMN task execution runs before anything is recorded: is the actor authenticated, assigned to the role the lane binds, authorized by an ODRL policy to perform the task, and allowed access to the content it acts on? One generic check in the engine rather than a step drawn in some diagrams; strict, with GitHub as the authenticator. Also how the HTTP routes ask the same policies. f47238f52ec0.content: . | Command line. No workflow in this checkout runs its command. | . As an API: its operation in the OpenAPI document and the MCP tool list of its layer. |   |   | . | install | cli: pip install pymupdf | . | runtime | python3, pymupdf | . | network | no | . | when to choose it |   | . | when | A listing needs a cover and the bytes are already held. It renders page 1 by default and calls that the cover, because page 1 is a determined answer and “the cover” is not — the same choice pdf-pages.py makes about sections. | . | limits | It decides nothing beyond the raster. WHICH documents get a cover, where the file lands, and what the catalogue must say about the derivation are the catalogue’s to declare — see the content core’s scripts/gen-covers.ts, which reads them from a layer’s catalogue and refuses to write bytes for a THUMBNAIL that does not declare itself derived. It also cannot tell you whether the page it rendered IS the cover; it can only tell you it is page 1. | . | cost | One PyMuPDF wheel, no network at run time, and a few milliseconds per page. Deterministic — identical input gives identical bytes, which is what lets a caller gate on --check rather than re-deciding. | .

b88350cf3dd7.content: For each table a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json lists under tables, rewrites the block’s Markdown table from an archimate-relationship-rules/v1 file (relationship-rules: source, relationship, target, note; relationship-types: picture, verb, meaning), keeping the caption and footnotes. 1ecba589de60.title: Is this repository’s cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
1ecba589de60.content: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: mounts (every declared layer on disk at its pin — remote-mount --check), declarations (every path a declaration names resolves — declaration-resolution), monorepo-paths (no wiring still names the monorepo: livesAt on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), import-direction and reference-direction (no layer reaches a layer above it), and site (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — build-instance-site --no-mount, only with --site). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without --site the answer is never 0. |   |   | . | Tool | separation-cutover-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check/separation-cutover-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

63973b1c9b1c.title: Lower the tangles in ArchiMate views: re-route lines and swap same-size boxes in a row
63973b1c9b1c.content: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. Without --apply it reports before and after per view; with it, the model is written back in place, only the moved boxes’ bounds and the re-routed lines’ bendpoints changing. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-detangle | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-detangle.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-detangle/archimate-detangle.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1d21c271193c.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. 4680bd7284d0.title: Replay a committed mount lock with nothing but Node
4680bd7284d0.content: Lay down every remote mount index.lock.json records — each layer fetched at the lock’s full SHA (sparse, blob-filtered), each directory verified against its treeDigest, a mismatch undone and reported — importing only node:*, so it runs on a fresh clone before any layer is present. It never decides what to mount: remote-mount writes the lock (and checks trust); this only replays it. Refuses to write over a path with tracked files or bytes that no longer hash to the lock. f6e1c1f1a3ed.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, instantiate-harness, kg-retrieve-npm, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: declaration-resolution, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json).

3176a5ca09eb.title: Check declared credential needs against workflow use and expiry, by name
3176a5ca09eb.content: Compare each repository’s declared credential needs (credentials/needs.json, profile and registry) with the secrets.NAME expressions its workflows reference (GitHub Actions’ dollar-and-double-brace form, said in words because this text is rendered on a Jekyll page), with the secret names GitHub lists when a token allows it, and with any recorded expiry. NAMES ONLY — no value is ever read. Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0. |   |   | . | Tool | secrets-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/secrets-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/secrets-check/secrets-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

00e992395b53.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-adjudication.md. Also satisfied by: github, translation-adjudicate, translation-adjudication-workflow, translation-status-viewer. 986e2ac3016a.title: Apply a vocabulary mapping table
986e2ac3016a.content: Carry one source record into a target vocabulary by a declared folio-vocab-mapping/v1 table: each source field becomes the predicate its row names, in the table’s order, with a DERIVED target (such as dcterms:title rendering skos:prefLabel) copied from its authoritative one so the two cannot drift. A table is shaped like a FHIR ConceptMap: an existing ConceptMap, R4 or R5, is representable as one without loss (fromConceptMap), and a table can be produced as a ConceptMap (toConceptMap), which returns every loss rather than dropping anything silently. 6c3899169b53.title: Skills it satisfies
6c3899169b53.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s word on a translation, carried from the translation review page or a block’s 🌐 pane to the record: anyone proposes text, which joins the ranked candidates; an owner, member or collaborator adjudicates, by accepting a catalogue or choosing one string’s translation with a reason; it is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records, re-runs the auto-pick and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. Use for “review the translations”, “this string is mistranslated”, “why was my review not recorded”, and when wiring a layer for review. Locale sign-off is a separate act, not this one. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-adjudication.md. Also satisfied by: translation-adjudicate, translation-adjudication-workflow, translation-review-page, translation-status-viewer. 222b3027fa04.title: Give every page Jekyll did not lay out the folio-assistant navbar

ba7d858d7ff2.title: Convert a checkout to a root index.config.json
ba7d858d7ff2.content: Write the root index.config.json (folio-index-config/v1) that says which layers the checkout instantiates, where each comes from (source.local or source.remote) and which owns / (site.landing), from the root *.config.json files and the declaration’s remoteMounts. With --write it moves remoteMounts off the declaration into source.remote entries, writes the generated .gitignore block, and renames a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json to index.lock.json. Without a flag it prints the index it would write. Idempotent: a re-run merges what the declaration gained, and refuses an entry the index already holds differently. A root config naming no layer is reported as unmatched-config and not imported, because what to do with it is a person’s decision. |   |   | . | Tool | index-config-migrate | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/index-config-migrate.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/index-config-migrate/index-config-migrate.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. dfdfe705d4d0.title: Skills it satisfies
dfdfe705d4d0.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: instantiate-harness. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). getting-started . Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in a layer that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or “folio-assistant” itself. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/getting-started.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/getting-started/{input,output}.schema.json). folio-init . Scaffold a new folio layer from the harness — the instantiate affordance of the knowledge graph. Covers when to run folio-init vs remote-mount, what the scaffold writes, the builder shim, state branch seeding, write capability requirements, and –dry-run degradation. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/folio-init.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/folio-init/{input,output}.schema.json).

Package, release, distribute, and retrieve Knowledge Graphs using npm tooling and tarballs: declare package.json as an authored pre-packaging asset in the Knowledge Graph, build .tgz packages via bun pm pack, record publications as folio-binary-release/v1 state documents hosted on GitHub binary releases, and retrieve remote Knowledge Graphs using npm install for both unhydrated source graph and hydrated materialized graph views. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/npm-kg-distribution.md. Also satisfied by: ci-publish-subgraph-index, npm, pack-tarball, package-release-manual, package-release-workflow, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/npm-kg-distribution/{input,output}.schema.json). remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, instantiate-harness, mount-from-lock, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json).

076242ba4ac4.content: Drop the translation-semantic-roundtrip rulings of strings the catalogues no longer hold, and renumber the rest to catalogue order. f561eec016f6.title: Skills it satisfies
f561eec016f6.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-manager . Translation lifecycle management for folio content. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, the poSources fallback resolution chain, and translating into several locales as a team: one extraction, a PR per locale to main, FHIR terms as CodeSystem supplements, the untainted round trip as run, and the per-locale QA report. c076f434e543.title: DAK task annotations → BPMN sidecars
c076f434e543.content: Read a DAK document’s per-task “NOTES AND ANNOTATIONS” from its L1 section text (who-iris), match each numbered item to the BPMN task it describes (by @id, then the label’s step number with the file’s process letter, then the name), add the persona from the task’s lane or pool and the data elements, functional requirements and decision tables the DAK workbooks key to the activity id, and write one dak-task-annotations/v1 sidecar (<file>.tasks.json) beside each BPMN (smart-base/L2-bpmn/scripts/dak-task-annotations.ts, schema smart-base/L2-bpmn/schemas/task-annotations.ts). Items no task matches are listed for a person to adjudicate; a re-run keeps adjudicated matches. --report prints what a set of sidecars covers and never fails. The BPMN is read, never written, and nothing FHIR-specific is involved. |   |   | . | Tool | dak-task-annotations | . | IRI | http://smart.who.int/base/tools/dak-task-annotations.jsonld | . | part of | http://smart.who.int/base/smart-base.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | smart-base | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

64652b049b32.title: BPMN structure, vendor namespaces and lane → actor
64652b049b32.content: Check a DAK’s BPMN (validate.ts beside this file; bean folio-assistant-tgaj, which replaced four Python validators with it): well-formed XML whose root is <bpmn:definitions>, no Camunda or Zeebe namespace, no duplicate id, at least one process, no bpmn-moddle (bpmn-js) import warning; every process has a <laneSet>, every flow node sits in a lane, and lane ids are unique and valid FSH ids; and every innermost lane names its actor by id: its partitionElementRef (a top-level <bpmn:resource>), else its own id, matched exactly against the Instance: ids of the ActorDefinitions in the IG’s FSH (or JSON) and, for a harness process, the role ids of the mounted layers’ scenarios/roles.json. a9d60de5bbc6.title: Tools — smart-base
a9d60de5bbc6.content: The Tool nodes smart-base declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 23Tool nodes 12skills satisfied 23invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

c0a9a532ae6c.title: Tools
c0a9a532ae6c.content: As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 249Tool nodes 97skills satisfied 224invoked as a shell command 23reachable over MCP

224fa1705a00.title: Every process — one page each

This section reported them as defects in its first version, and that was wrong: beans luke and uuhu worked this corpus from 90 down to this remainder and settled what is left. luke: “coverage is deliberately NOT gated — a human sign-off step has no skill”. uuhu added the call-activity exemption and recorded that its own remainder “are not gaps”. 12 are call activities, which delegate to a subprocess — the skill is named there, and naming it twice would be one fact in two places. 77a51d1400b4.title: indicator-extraction
77a51d1400b4.content: Skill indicator-extraction: Extract the indicators an L1 source prints (indicator reference or metadata sheets: name, numerator, denominator, disaggregation, definition, data sources) as L1 indicator nodes with every printed field, then draft one L2 program indicator per indicator, derived from its L1 node. Read before adding a WHO handbook’s or guideline’s indicators to a DAK or a DTH, and whenever an L2 indicator has to trace to its source. Part of L1 → L2 extraction for every DAK and DTH, beside recommendation-extraction. Named by: DTH authoring, L2 DAK authoring . Skill id: indicator-extraction · Package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines · Follows dak-l1-library, which ingests the source. Sibling of recommendation-extraction: that one takes a source’s recommendations, this one its indicators. It is a step of L1 → L2 extraction for a DAK or DTH, bound to Task_Indicators in l2-dak-authoring and Call_Data in dth-authoring.

602d6378b9e5.title: Two layers, kept apart
602d6378b9e5.content: | layer | what | kind / model | written by | . | L1 | the indicator as the source prints it, verbatim | indicator block (folio type smart-base:Indicator; KG L1 indicator, L1/schemas/l1.ts) | L1/scripts/l1-indicator-sheets.py → candidates.json → gen-library-jsonld | . | L2 | the DAK’s or DTH’s own operational measure, a draft that points back | program-indicator (sgkg-l2), logical model ProgramIndicator | scripts/l2-program-indicators.py | . sgkg-l2 keeps them apart: merging them would merge a WHO definition with a country’s implementation of it. The L2 record is a draft with derivedFrom its L1 node, and the L2 author adopts, edits or drops it.

e398779617e3.title: Rules
e398779617e3.content: . | Ids come from the source. number / indicatorId is the printed indicator number (“1-01”, “4-01.3”). A sheet whose header prints none is reported and skipped, never numbered by an agent. The L2 id is <prefix>.<number> (“NHWA.1-01”); the prefix only namespaces it. | Verbatim. Every field is the printed text: lines joined, letter-spacing artefacts closed up, nothing reworded. A printed list (glossary terms, data sources) is one string joined with “; “. | Every printed field, not only name, numerator and denominator. The L1 node’s meta holds indicatorId, module, abbreviatedName, name, numerator, denominator, disaggregation, definition, glossary, reportingFrequency, reportingFrameworks, dataSources, furtherInformation and dimension where printed; a sub-indicator adds parentIndicator and guidingQuestions. These are the keys the structured-block cards read. | No gap is filled. ProgramIndicator makes definition, numerator, denominator and disaggregation 1..1. Where the source prints none (a composite or self-assessed indicator), the L2 draft lists it in gaps and the L2 author decides. Nothing is copied from another source to fill it. | A composite indicator keeps its sub-indicators as their own L1 nodes; in L2 they are the parent’s components, not program indicators of their own. | Read the page layout, not the section text, when the source prints sheets as a label column and a value column: Stage A’s text reads side bars and columns out of order. | .

76ade665b93e.title: Steps
76ade665b93e.content: . | The source is in the library (dak-l1-library), with its PDF in uploads/<doc-id>/. | L1 candidates. From the library repository root: . python3 smart-base/L1/scripts/l1-indicator-sheets.py --entry library/<doc-id> \ --pdf uploads/<doc-id>/<doc-id>.pdf --pages <first>-<last> --json # look first python3 smart-base/L1/scripts/l1-indicator-sheets.py --entry library/<doc-id> \ --pdf uploads/<doc-id>/<doc-id>.pdf --pages <first>-<last> --write . --write merges into candidates.json as the indicators aspect, replacing an indicator candidate with the same number (re-runs are idempotent). Check the count against the source’s own list of indicators (NHWA: the synthesis table, 29 indicators). | L1 nodes. bun cat-harness-tools/pipeline/gen-library-jsonld.ts --entry library/<doc-id> writes blocks/indicator-<section>-NN.{jsonld,md}, each derivedFrom its section, provenance: ingested, with the fields in meta. Existing indicator IRIs do not change when the first candidate of a section stays the same indicator. | L2 drafts. python3 smart-base/scripts/l2-program-indicators.py --entry library/<doc-id> \ --prefix <PREFIX> --out <where the L2 author will review them> . | Into the DAK or DTH. The L2 author takes the drafts into the guide’s indicators component (DAK component 8; a DTH’s data elements, indicators and requirements), through the guide’s own review (l2-component-edit-review) and, for a DTH, a change set. | .

5e93e817990d.title: Validated against
5e93e817990d.content: . | NHWA handbook, 2nd edition (who-iris 9789240081291-eng): 29 indicators, 33 sub-indicators, PDF pages 51-91. | . Not yet run on a guideline whose indicator sheets use a different layout (HIV SI 2022’s reference sheets: “What it measures”, “Rationale”, “Method of measurement”). Those labels are in the script’s label list, but the header number pattern may need a per-source ID_PATTERN.

4df8e6f63ac3.title: Inform the client
4df8e6f63ac3.content: Skill inform-client: A health worker tells the client (or caregiver) what was decided and what happens next, in words and, where the DAK gives one, on a slip or card: a referral, a return date, a result. Input is what to tell and the client’s language; output is that the client was told, and what they were handed. Generic for any DAK step that ends with the client being informed. Named by: Act on decision-support guidance, Capture data with an SDC questionnaire . Skill id: inform-client · Package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines · Performed by a person in a health-worker lane. WHO’s immunization DAK has it as IMMZ.D7 “Counsel client” and IMMZ.D9 “Inform client when to return”.

69d80bd751f2.title: Input and output
69d80bd751f2.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In: the about (a referral, a return visit, a result, a decision), the facts to convey, the language the client understands, and any handout the DAK gives (a referral slip, a vaccination card). | Out: informed (true once said and understood), the handedOver items, and the questions the client raised that need follow-up. | .

5372b23c60cf.title: What the health worker does
5372b23c60cf.content: . | Say what was decided and what happens next, in the client’s language, without jargon; check it was understood. | Hand over the slip or card when the DAK gives one. | Note any question that needs a follow-up. Nothing else is recorded: this step adds no form. | .

9897faaf2c95.title: Success criteria
9897faaf2c95.content: . | The client can say where to go, when, and why. | Every handout the DAK names was given. | .

c9d352312fb3.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
c9d352312fb3.title: Steps
c9d352312fb3.content: Every one of the 7 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Write dublin-core.jsonld (the record of truth)Task_Dublin | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | One standalone Dublin Core record per folder. dcterms is already this corpus’s JSON-LD vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one. | . | Write manifest.jsonld referencing itTask_Manifest | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write manifest.jsonld for the folder: its @id, @type folio:SourceDocument, what it contains and its provenance, referencing the standalone dublin-core.jsonld as the record of truth rather than copying its fields. | . | Record assets[] — local path or remote URLTask_Assets | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | kind / role / url-or-path / checksum / retrieved. A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync. | . | Bind the folder to its bibliography slugTask_Bind | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Bind the folder name to the document’s bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. | . | Read glossary into candidate termsTask_Glossary | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | glossary-terms | The source’s glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. Terms a person owns are never changed, and only a person moves a term to authored. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written. | . | Extract reference listsTask_References | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Each reference list of the source (a References, Bibliography or Further reading section, in any of the six UN languages) becomes folio-reference/v1 nodes with the Tool references-extract: one node per cited work, provenance extracted, derivedFrom the section it was read from, and printed the entry exactly as the source prints it. Only fields read without guessing are set (address, DOI, ISBN, year, access date); a cited IRIS item the library holds gets heldAt. The nodes are the document’s own bibliography on the bibliography page. A source with no reference list skips this step with nothing written. | . | Link L1 nodes into the corpus graphTask_Link | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact – paper, L2, L3 – resolves to it through library/. | .

3c749f2c2990.title: Steps
3c749f2c2990.content: Every one of the 8 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Archive → greppable contents manifestTask_Archive | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library’s image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Transcribe and translate audioTask_Audio | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | No Tool yet; the method, and the choice of recogniser, is skill audio-transcription. | . | Sheet names, headers, shape, narrativeTask_Tabular | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Tools tabular-csv and tabular-xlsx, as CSVW (skill tabular-metadata). CSV and spreadsheet: tabs, column and row headers, sizes, and what the dataset is about. | . | Extract figures and tablesTask_FiguresTables | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The pdf-images.py, pdf-vector-labels.py and pdf-vector-figures.py arms extract the raster images and the figures drawn as vectors (grouped and rendered). For every table the document’s structure declares, an agent reads the rendered page, checks cell text against the text layer, and writes tables/<label>.csv plus tables.csvw.json (folio-tabular-csvw/v1), with a draft description in the six UN languages; pdf-tables.py’s grid is a cross-check, not the answer. Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris): “actually extract the figures” and “any tables too”. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Footnotes and the marks that call themTask_Footnotes | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | The pdf-footnotes.py arm (owner, 2026-11-11, “also foot notes/marks”): from the page layout, each note at the foot of a page and every superscript mark in the text that calls it, written to footnotes.json (folio-document-footnotes/v1) with the block that holds the page. The section text is not changed. Only a called note is a footnote; uncalled foot-of-page lines and marks with no note are listed, never dropped. OCR’d pages have no fonts and are reported unread. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “Footnotes and their marks”. | . | Cite the author of every narrativeTask_Provenance | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | A generated description is a claim by someone. Record whether a human or an agent wrote it, and for an agent the model version. An uncited narrative is indistinguishable from a transcription of the source. | .

78e4c076dc79.title: Steps
78e4c076dc79.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract the text layerTask_ExtractText | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. | . | Check each page; OCR pages that failTask_PageCheck | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris, card Q-ODD-1 = A): “force OCR when a page’s text layer fails a quality check”. A text layer can hold plenty of letters and still not be the page’s text: accents mapped to Greek letters (“dΘclaration”), Persian set in the wrong Arabic code points, words split by kerning (“au g m ente”), fake-bold words printed twice, mojibake. cat-harness-tools scripts/_text_quality.py checks every page against the document’s languages (dc.language.iso, or –lang-hint); the router then OCRs the document and pdf-structure.py –ocr takes the OCR text for the failing pages only, listing them in structure.json source.ocr_pages with the reason. When most pages of a document with no outline fail, the whole document is read from OCR, as for a scan. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “A text layer that is not text”. | . | OCR to ocr/page-*.txtTask_Ocr | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Each page is read in the document’s languages (–lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article’s Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document’s references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently (“Manual” and “Manval”), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. | . | Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matterTask_Sections | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief. An outline is set aside when its entries are machine bookmark names (_GoBack, _Hlk…, “Blank Page”, a merged file’s name) or when under half of them name a heading the pages print, and the contents are inferred instead (diagnostics.outline_rejected). A section that would hold more than half of a document of 20 pages or more (and over 8,000 words), or over 20,000 words anywhere, is cut at the headings inferred inside it, else one section per page (diagnostics.oversized_split). Owner, 2026-11-11: “split single blocks that hold a whole book”. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “An outline that is not contents, and a section too long to be a block”. | . | Write structure.jsonTask_Structure | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR’d text, source.runContext cites the OCR step’s run context by sha256. A title already known for the document (the catalogue’s dc.title, or one given with –title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections’ doc_title does not carry a scan’s misreading. | . | Extract claim candidatesTask_Candidates | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only – never adjudicated verdicts. | .
